definition_zh: 诈骗；骗取（钱财）；（名词）骗局；诈骗行为
definition_en: to get money or property from someone by tricking them, often with a bold scheme
core_image: 街头摆着一张金光闪闪的转盘，庄家笑眯眯地请路人下注，转盘转完，路人的钱包已经空了
scene: 集市尽头的摊位上，穿西装的男人拍着胸脯保证「稳赚三倍」，几个老人围上去数钱。A smooth salesman swindled half the village out of their savings.
sceneCN: 这里 swindle 是「诈骗、骗取钱财」（第 1 个义项：用诡计骗走财物）；句意：一个能说会道的推销员骗走了半个村子的积蓄。

collocations.phrase: swindle somebody out of their savings
be swindled by a fake offer

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -er 构成，义为「骗子；诈骗犯」
动词加 -ing 构成，义为「诈骗行为」
过去分词转形容词，义为「被骗的」

senses.title: To cheat someone out of money
senses.definition: to take money or property from a person by means of a trick, a false promise, or a dishonest scheme
senses.definitionCN: 用诡计、虚假承诺或不诚实的计划拿走他人的钱财或财物
senses.example: Two men swindled her out of her pension with a fake insurance deal.
senses.exampleCN: 两个男人用一份假的保险交易骗走了她的养老金。
senses.why: The word grew out of a German term for a giddy, unsteady turn, so swindling is money made to walk in circles until it lands in the wrong pocket.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源于德语中表示「头晕、打转」的说法，所以诈骗就是让钱在原地打转，最后落进别人口袋。

senses.title: To trick people into a bad deal
senses.definition: to persuade someone with lies to accept an unfair bargain, even when money is not the main thing taken
senses.definitionCN: 用谎言说服他人接受不公平的交易，即便被拿走的不主要是钱
senses.example: The dealer swindled the tourists into buying fake brand bags.
senses.exampleCN: 这个商贩哄骗游客买下了假的名牌包。
senses.why: Since the trick rather than the cash was the heart of the word, English let it cover any unfair bargain, not only stolen money.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心是「设局」而非「现金」，所以英语让它覆盖任何不公平的交易，而不限于骗钱。

senses.title: A dishonest scheme as a noun
senses.definition: a fraudulent scheme, or the act of deceiving people in order to take their money
senses.definitionCN: 骗取钱财的欺诈性计划，或指诈骗这一行为
senses.example: The police are investigating a swindle that cost residents thousands.
senses.exampleCN: 警方正在调查一起让居民损失数千的骗局。
senses.why: As the verb spread, the noun was re-formed in the nineteenth century to name the scheme itself, the thing a swindler runs.
senses.whyCN: 随着动词流行，十九世纪重新构出名词，专指骗局本身，也就是骗子所经营的那套计划。

senses.title: To be a swindler or to work by fraud
senses.definition: an intransitive use meaning to practise fraud, or to make a living by deceiving others
senses.definitionCN: 不及物用法，指从事欺诈，或以欺骗他人为生
senses.example: For years he swindled from town to town under many names.
senses.exampleCN: 多年来他化名多端，在一个个城镇之间行骗。
senses.why: The same verb could describe the habit rather than one act, so English allows it to stand alone without a victim named.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词也能描述习性而非单次行为，所以英语允许它单独使用，不点明受害者。

intro.en: Swindle is probably from German schwindeln, related to a root for giddiness; the path through German is likely but not proven.
intro.cn: swindle 一般认为来自德语 schwindeln，与表示「头晕」的词根有关；经由德语传入这一说法较可信，但未完全证实。

items.en: A root group meaning to swoon or grow dizzy is generally reconstructed; the deeper Proto-Indo-European source is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为存在一个表示「晕倒、头晕」的词根群；更早的原始印欧语来源不确定。

items.en: Schwindeln means to be giddy, or to tell fibs. Lie and light-headedness met in one word, and the older senses survive in German today.
items.cn: schwindeln 意为「头晕」，也指「说小谎」；谎言与头晕在同一个词里相遇，这些旧义至今保存在德语中。

items.en: Swindling is recorded in English in the eighteenth century, first in the cant and trading language of London.
items.cn: 十八世纪英语中出现 swindling，最初流行于伦敦的方言黑话与生意圈。

items.en: The noun swindle was formed from the verb, and the word spread to courts, newspapers, and commerce.
items.cn: 十九世纪由动词构出名词 swindle，这个词扩展到法庭、报纸与商业领域。

items.en: Middle Low German swindeln offers a closely related form, which supports the German origin but leaves the exact route uncertain.
items.cn: 中古低地德语 swindeln 是关系很近的形式，这支持德语来源说，但确切传入路线仍不确定。

items.en: Modern English uses swindle for financial fraud, from small street cons to large investment schemes.
items.cn: 现代英语用 swindle 指金融诈骗，从街头小骗局到大型投资骗局都涵盖。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers kin from the German dizzy family and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers fraud words by register and seriousness.
note.cn: 形近组收源自德语「头晕」一族的亲族词与近形拼写；近义组按语体与严重程度收「欺诈」类词。

entries.definition: a person who cheats others out of money by trickery.
entries.definitionCN: 用诡计骗走他人钱财的人。

entries.definition: the act of cheating people out of money.
entries.definitionCN: 诈骗行为。

entries.definition: an old traders term for a list of doubtful customers; merely close in shape to the modern word.
entries.definitionCN: 旧时的商贩用语，指可疑顾客名单；只是外形相近，用法不同。

entries.definition: to take money from someone by deceit, usually said in law.
entries.definitionCN: 以欺骗手段取走他人钱财，多用于法律语体。

entries.definition: to trick someone, especially a stranger, into giving money for nothing.
entries.definitionCN: 诈骗某人，尤指陌生人，以骗取钱财。

entries.definition: a dishonest plan, often online, that takes money from many people at once.
entries.definitionCN: 不诚实的骗局，常在网上，一次性骗走很多人的钱。

normalIntro.en: Swindle is a dizzy word for deception: the victim is spun round until the money changes hands.
normalIntro.cn: swindle 是一个「头晕」的欺骗词：受害者被转得晕头转向，钱就换了主人。

normal.en: He swindled his neighbour out of a large sum.
normal.cn: 他骗走了邻居一大笔钱。

normal.en: A swindler runs a swindle and gets swindled in the end only under a hotter scheme.
normal.cn: 骗子从事骗局，往往只有更大的骗局才能骗倒他。

normal.en: Note the out of in swindle somebody out of something.
normal.cn: 注意搭配 swindle somebody out of something 中的 out of。

normal.en: Compare scam, which is more casual and often online, while swindle sounds older and more serious.
normal.cn: 对比 scam：scam 更口语、多在网上，swindle 听起来更古老、更严肃。

normal.en: The German origin links lying with dizziness, so the word carries both a lie and a spin.
normal.cn: 德语来源把谎言与头晕连在一起，所以这个词同时带着「谎言」与「打转」。

abstract.en: Picture a spinning lottery wheel that nobody but the dealer understands.
abstract.cn: 想象一台只有庄家看得懂的转盘抽奖机。

abstract.en: Imagine a wallet passing through many smiling hands and coming back empty.
abstract.cn: 想象一个钱包在许多笑呵呵的手之间传递，回来时空空如也。

abstract.en: Think of a contract with tiny words in the corner that undo the big promise at the top.
abstract.cn: 想象一份合同，角落的小字推翻了开头的大承诺。

examples.en: The couple swindled elderly neighbours out of their life savings.
examples.cn: 这对夫妇骗光了老年邻居的毕生积蓄。

examples.en: It took the auditors three years to expose the swindle.
examples.cn: 审计人员花了三年才揭穿这个骗局。

examples.en: Anyone offered such returns should suspect a swindle.
examples.cn: 任何人碰到这样的回报，都应怀疑其中有诈。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死吻的」——骗子先用甜言蜜语把你「吻」晕，钱就没了；这是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 原始日耳曼语「晕倒」词根 → 德语 schwindeln（头晕；说小谎）→ 中古低地德语 swindeln → 英语 swindle（诈骗）；核心义「把人转晕，骗走财物」。

sensesIntro.en: Swindle begins as cheating money out of people, widens to unfair bargains, becomes the name of the scheme itself in the nineteenth century, and can even stand alone for the habit of fraud.
sensesIntro.cn: swindle 从「骗走钱财」出发，扩展到「哄骗人做亏本交易」，十九世纪又名词化为「骗局」，还能单独指「行骗这一习性」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spinning wheel where the crowd loses and the dealer wins.
core.cn: 核心意象：转盘停下，众人输钱，庄家赢钱。

branches.en: Taking money by trick is the core everyday sense.
branches.cn: 用诡计拿走钱财是核心的日常义。

branches.en: Any unfair bargain won by lies belongs here too.
branches.cn: 任何靠谎言赢来的不公平交易也属于此。

branches.en: The noun names the scheme rather than the act.
branches.cn: 名词义指骗局这套计划，而非单次行为。

branches.en: Money and bargains are both taken by the same spin.
branches.cn: 骗钱与骗交易都出自同一种「转晕」的手法。

branches.en: The scheme and the habit of fraud describe the swindler from two sides.
branches.cn: 骗局与行骗习性从两个侧面描写骗子。

intro.en: Swindle has no Latin root; German built schwindeln from a dizzying verb, and English added swindler and swindling.
intro.cn: swindle 没有拉丁词根；德语从表示「头晕」的动词构出 schwindeln，英语再加 -er 与 -ing 构成 swindler 与 swindling。

latinIntro.en: There is no attested Latin source; the word travelled through German, so Latin entries are left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有证据支持拉丁语来源；该词经由德语传入，因此拉丁同源词留空。

items.example: Schwindeln links dizziness with lying.
items.exampleCN: schwindeln 把头晕与说谎连在一起。

items.example: Swindeln is the closest cousin to the English word.
items.exampleCN: swindeln 是英语词的最近亲族。

items.example: Swindle keeps its German dizziness.
items.exampleCN: swindle 保留了德语的「头晕」意象。

items.example: The suffix -er forms swindler.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 swindler。

items.example: A swindler works by charm and tricks.
items.exampleCN: 骗子靠魅力与诡计行事。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms swindling.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 swindling。

items.example: Swindling is often punished by long sentences.
items.exampleCN: 诈骗常被判处长期徒刑。

items.example: The pattern out of marks what is taken away.
items.exampleCN: 搭配中的 out of 标出被拿走的东西。

definition_zh: （使）旋转；转动；（以某物为轴）回身；（名词）旋转接头；转轴；转椅
definition_en: to turn or make something turn on a central point, or a joint that allows such turning
core_image: 办公椅底下的转轴一压就转，人轻轻一蹬，整个身体连人带椅转向窗边
scene: 灯塔顶端的探照灯架在一根轴上，夜里它缓慢地转着，灰光扫过海面与礁石。The lamp on the lighthouse swivelled slowly across the dark water.
sceneCN: 这里 swivel 是「旋转、转动」（第 1 个义项：绕轴转动）；句意：灯塔上的灯在漆黑的海面上缓缓转动。

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -ing 转形容词，义为「旋转的；可转动的」
swivel 加紧接式复合成分构成，义为「装在三脚转轴上的」
由动词加名词构成的复合词，义为「转椅」

senses.title: To turn on a central point
senses.definition: to turn around a fixed middle point, or to make something turn in this way
senses.definitionCN: 绕一个固定的中心点转动，或使某物这样转动
senses.example: The telescope swivels on a heavy iron base.
senses.exampleCN: 望远镜在沉重的铁底座上转动。
senses.why: The word began as a joint that pivots, so turning is its oldest and most physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指让东西转动的接头，所以「转动」是它最古老也最具体的义项。

senses.title: To turn the body or head round
senses.definition: to turn your body or head quickly to look in another direction
senses.definitionCN: 迅速转身或扭头朝另一个方向看
senses.example: She swivelled round to catch the door before it slammed.
senses.exampleCN: 她迅速转身，在门关上之前住了手。
senses.why: A body on its feet works like a chair on a pivot, so the same verb slipped easily onto people.
senses.whyCN: 双脚站着的身体就像转轴上的椅子，同一个动词于是很自然地用到了人身上。

senses.title: A turning joint or axle
senses.definition: a joint, ring, or pin built so that the part fixed to it can rotate freely
senses.definitionCN: 一种接头、圆环或销轴，装在其上的部件可以自由转动
senses.example: Replace the rusted swivel before the line is used again.
senses.exampleCN: 再次使用吊索之前，先换掉生锈的旋转接头。
senses.why: The noun sense came first, naming the hard little joint; English then made the verb out of it.
senses.whyCN: 名词义其实更早，指那个坚硬的小接头；英语再由它造出动词。

senses.title: A chair or device that turns
senses.definition: a chair, stand, or mount fitted so that the user can sit and turn in it
senses.definitionCN: 装有转轴、使用者可以坐着转身的椅子、支架或底座
senses.example: He pulled the swivel up to the desk and started typing.
senses.exampleCN: 他把转椅拉到桌前，开始打字。
senses.why: Short for swivel chair, the noun now names the furniture, not just the joint inside it.
senses.whyCN: 作为 swivel chair 的省略形式，名词现在指整件家具，而不只是里面的转轴。

intro.en: Swivel comes through Middle English from an Old English root meaning to swivel or sweep round; the deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: swivel 经中古英语来自古英语中表示「打转、扫转」的词根；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: A root group meaning to swing or turn is generally reconstructed; its deeper Proto-Indo-European ancestor is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为存在一个表示「摆动、转动」的词根群；更早的原始印欧语祖形不确定。

items.en: The verb swifan meant to sweep, turn, or move round, and it survives only in related forms today.
items.cn: 古英语动词 swifan 意为「扫转、转动、环绕」，今天只存活在相关形式里。

items.en: The noun swivel appears in the fourteenth century, a small ring or collar that lets a rope turn without twisting; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 名词 swivel 见于十四世纪，指让绳索转动而不打绞的小圆环或套环；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the verb swivel is recorded, applied to joints, guns, and anchored things that turn.
items.cn: 到十六世纪已见动词 swivel，用于接头、火炮以及固定住却能转动的东西。

items.en: The swivel chair, said to have been used by Thomas Jefferson, made the word a household piece of office furniture.
items.cn: 据说杰斐逊用过的转椅，让 swivel chair 成为家喻户晓的办公家具。

items.en: Modern English uses swivel freely for heads, cameras, and screens that turn, and the double l spelling is now mostly British.
items.cn: 现代英语把 swivel 自由用于能转动的头、摄像头与屏幕；双写 l 的拼法如今多见于英式英语。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same turning root and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers the main words for turning by kind of motion.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「转动」词族的词与近形拼写；近义组按动作类型收主要的「转动」词。

entries.definition: an office chair whose seat turns on a post.
entries.definitionCN: 座面可绕立柱转动的办公椅。

entries.definition: a pipe joint that lets the parts turn at any angle.
entries.definitionCN: 允许部件任意角度转动的管道接头。

entries.definition: a soft sweeping movement or sound; merely spelled alike and from another root.
entries.definitionCN: 轻快拂过的动作或声音；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: to turn all the way round a centre, as a wheel does.
entries.definitionCN: 像轮子一样绕中心整整转一圈。

entries.definition: to turn on one small point, the way a door turns on its hinge.
entries.definitionCN: 绕一个小点转动，像门绕铰链那样。

entries.definition: to turn something round and round on itself, often to wind it.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物自身拧转，常指缠绕。

normalIntro.en: Swivel is the joint word: a fixed middle, a free outer ring, and anything that can turn on it.
normalIntro.cn: swivel 是「接头」词：中间固定，外圈自由，凡能装在上面转的都由它来说。

normal.en: The lamp swivels on a small base.
normal.cn: 台灯在一个小底座上转动。

normal.en: British spelling doubles the l in swivelled and swivelling.
normal.cn: 英式拼写在 swivelled 与 swivelling 中双写 l。

normal.en: A swivel chair takes its name from the hidden joint below the seat.
normal.cn: swivel chair 得名于座位下面看不见的转轴。

normal.en: Swivel often takes on or round: it swivels on its base, she swivels round.
normal.cn: swivel 常接 on 或 round：it swivels on its base、she swivels round。

normal.en: Compare rotate, which goes all the way round, while swivel turns freely to a new direction.
normal.cn: 对比 rotate：rotate 是整圈转，swivel 是自由转向新方向。

abstract.en: Picture a radar dish sweeping the same circle night after night.
abstract.cn: 想象雷达天线一夜又一夜扫着同一个圆圈。

abstract.en: Imagine someone on a bar stool swinging round to answer a call.
abstract.cn: 想象有人坐在高脚凳上一转，回过身去接电话。

abstract.en: Think of a pin that holds two things together yet lets them turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一根销轴，把两样东西固定在一起，却允许它们转动。

examples.en: The monitor swivels so that either of us can read it.
examples.cn: 显示器可以转动，我们两人都看得见。

examples.en: He swivelled in his chair to face the window.
examples.cn: 他在椅子上转过身面对窗户。

examples.en: The swivel under the seat had rusted, so the chair no longer swivelled.
examples.cn: 座位下面的转轴锈住了，椅子再也转不动了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死围了」——人被围在中间转不动；反过来记：中间的轴「死」钉住，外圈才「围」着它转。这是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 日耳曼语「摆动、转动」词根 → 古英语 swifan（扫转、环绕）→ 中古英语 swivel（可转动的环）→ 英语 swivel（旋转接头；转动）；核心义「固定轴上的自由转动」。

sensesIntro.en: Swivel starts as a small turning joint, becomes a verb for anything that turns on such a joint, and then stretches from machines to heads, and from joints to the chairs that contain them.
sensesIntro.cn: swivel 从一个小小旋转接头出发，变成「绕这样的接头转动」的动词，再从机器扩展到人的头，从接头扩展到装着接头的椅子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an office chair swinging round on a small hidden pivot.
core.cn: 核心意象：办公椅绕看不见的转轴转过去。

branches.en: Turning on a fixed point is the plain mechanical sense.
branches.cn: 绕固定点转动是朴素的机械义。

branches.en: Heads and bodies turn on the same kind of pivot.
branches.cn: 头与身体的转动用的是同一类转轴。

branches.en: The joint itself is the oldest noun sense.
branches.cn: 接头本身是最早的名词义。

branches.en: Machine and body alike need a fixed centre to turn about.
branches.cn: 机器与身体一样，都需要一个固定的中心才能转。

branches.en: A swivel chair invites the body to turn, so the furniture and the gesture meet.
branches.cn: 转椅邀请身体转动，于是家具与动作在此相遇。

intro.en: Swivel is a native Germanic turning word with no Latin root; English built swivelling, swivel chair, and swivel-mounted on it by suffix and compounding.
intro.cn: swivel 是本土日耳曼语的「转动」词，没有拉丁词根；英语用后缀与合成为它造出 swivelling、swivel chair 与 swivel-mounted。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source is attested for this word family; Latin turning words such as torquere are only distant cousins in meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 这一词族没有证据支持拉丁语来源；拉丁语中表示「拧转」的 torquere 等词只在意义上算远亲。

items.example: Swifan is the old turning root behind the word.
items.exampleCN: swifan 是该词背后古老的「转动」词根。

items.example: The first swivel was a ring for a rope.
items.exampleCN: 最早的 swivel 是给绳索用的圆环。

items.example: The verb swivel grew out of the joint.
items.exampleCN: 动词 swivel 由接头一词生长出来。

items.meaningCN: 构成分词或形容词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms swivelling.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 swivelling。

items.example: Swivelling describes a turning part.

items.example: Swivel-mounted screens are common in studios.

items.example: Swivel joint names the mechanics plainly.

definition_zh: 指不同地区常见的三种大树：欧亚异叶槭（假挪威槭）；美洲悬铃木；中东与非洲的无花果类乔木（西克莫无花果）
definition_en: a name shared by several large trees, especially the maple with mottled bark in Britain, the plane tree in North America, and a fig tree of the eastern Mediterranean
core_image: 一棵大树站在村口：粗干、宽冠，树皮剥落后露出浅色斑块
scene: 乡间公路的拐角处，两个路人停下脚步，抬头打量路旁那棵高大的树。The old sycamore at the corner was shedding its bark, leaving pale patches on the trunk.
sceneCN: 这里 sycamore 指的是「欧亚异叶槭」（第 1 个义项：英国常见的假挪威槭）；句意：拐角处那棵老槭树正在掉树皮，树干上留下浅色斑块。

pos.zh: 异叶槭；假挪威槭（英国常称 sycamore，树皮脱落呈斑驳浅色）
美洲悬铃木（北美用语，对应英国口径中的 plane tree）
西克莫无花果；埃及无花果（中东与东非的一类无花果属乔木，圣经植物）

derivatives.zh: sycamore 的另一种常用拼写（尤见于邮票、地名与旧文献）
西卡明；圣经英译中的另一树名（一般认为指黑桑），si- 与 camine 拼写相近，容易与 sycamore 混看
带槭叶样式的（如槭叶形图样、纹章上的三叶或五裂叶纹）

senses.title: The maple with mottled bark
senses.definition: a large European maple with five-lobed leaves and bark that peels to show pale patches
senses.definitionCN: 欧洲一种大型槭树，叶子五裂，树皮剥落露出浅色斑块
senses.example: The sycamore at the edge of the field was planted long before the house.
senses.exampleCN: 田边那棵槭树比这所房子早得多就种下了。
senses.why: The name drifted to this maple through popular usage, though the ancient tree it once named was a fig; the mixed history is why one English term now covers several species.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字是经民间使用漂移到异叶槭身上的，而它最初所指的古树其实是无花果；正因这段混杂的历史，一个英语词如今覆盖了好几种树。

senses.title: The American plane tree
senses.definition: the plane tree of eastern North America, whose bark also flakes away in pale patches
senses.definitionCN: 北美东部的一种悬铃木，树皮同样会剥落成浅色斑块
senses.example: A sycamore lined the creek where the boys swam.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩们游泳的小溪两岸生长着悬铃木。
senses.why: North American speakers noticed the same flaking bark as their British neighbours, so North American speakers, unlike British ones, give the ancient name to a plane tree.
senses.whyCN: 北美说话人注意到和白人邻居一样的树皮剥落现象，于是美国人口中的这个名字落在了悬铃木身上，而英国人口中并非如此。

senses.title: The fig of the Bible lands
senses.definition: a large fig tree of the eastern Mediterranean whose fruits grow in clusters on the trunk and branches
senses.definitionCN: 地中海东部一种大型无花果树，果实成簇长在树干和枝条上
senses.example: The tax collector climbed the sycamore to see over the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 税吏爬上了那棵无花果树，好越过人群看个清楚。
senses.why: The Hebrew term the Greeks borrowed pointed at a fruit tree, so the oldest layer of the word is a fig with a thick trunk and sweet hanging fruit.
senses.whyCN: 希腊人借入的希伯来语词指的是果树，所以这个词最古老的一层就是那种树干粗壮、果实低垂味甜的无花果。

senses.title: A tree for a place and a street
senses.definition: a single old tree that people use as a meeting place, a parish boundary, or the name of a site
senses.definitionCN: 某处一棵上了年纪的大树，人们把它当作碰头地点、教区界标或地名来源
senses.example: The old sycamore marks the line between the two villages.
senses.exampleCN: 那棵老槭树标出了两个村庄之间的界线。
senses.why: A big tree stands still and is seen from far away, so villages gave it the power of a landmark and a name.
senses.whyCN: 大树静止不动，又远看可见，于是村子把地标与命名的功能交给了它。

senses.title: The wood of the tree
senses.definition: the pale, hard timber of the sycamore maple, used for furniture, bowls, and musical instruments
senses.definitionCN: 假挪威槭浅色坚硬的木材，用于家具、木碗和乐器
senses.example: The bowl was carved from a single block of sycamore.
senses.exampleCN: 那只碗是用一整块槭木雕出来的。
senses.why: Once people chop the tree they hold the wood, so the name of the living plant becomes the name of its pale, close-grained material.
senses.whyCN: 树一被砍倒，人手里握住的就是木材，于是活树的名称顺势变成了那种浅色细密木料的名称。

senses.title: The word in a place name
senses.definition: part of a British road, farm, or parish name that records where such trees once stood
senses.definitionCN: 英国路名、农庄名或教区名的一部分，记录着那里曾经的槭树
senses.example: The road called Sycamore Lane still has one tree of its own.
senses.exampleCN: 那条叫「槭树巷」的路至今还留着一棵自家的树。
senses.why: Land names hold things that last; when the trees are gone the word survives on the signpost as a fossil of the landscape.
senses.whyCN: 地名的保有性很强，树没了，词还留在路牌上，成了旧景观的化石。

intro.en: Sycamore comes through Latin sycomorus and Greek sykomoros from a Semitic word for a fig tree; the tree it named in Palestine was not the maple we now call by this name.
intro.cn: sycamore 经由拉丁语 sycomorus、希腊语 sykomoros，来自闪米特语中指无花果树的一个词；它在巴勒斯坦指的那棵树，并不是今天英语里叫这个名字的槭树。

items.en: The Hebrew term shiqmah names a fig tree of Palestine; its exact origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 希伯来语 shiqmah 指巴勒斯坦的一种无花果树，它的确切来源不确定。

items.en: Greek took the name as sykomoros and explained it, by folk etymology, as sykon, fig, plus moron, mulberry.
items.cn: 希腊语借作 sykomoros，并按民间词源把它拆成 sykon（无花果）加 moron（桑）。

items.en: Latin adopted the Greek name as sycomorus for the fig of Egypt and Syria.
items.cn: 拉丁语沿用希腊语作 sycomorus，指埃及与叙利亚的无花果。

items.en: Old French brought the word in as sicamor, and later forms settled into sycomore.
items.cn: 古法语把它带入作 sicamor，后来的形式逐渐写定为 sycomore。

items.en: English records sycomore as the biblical fig; a separate line of the word, often written sycamore, became common for the fig-like plane and the maple.
items.cn: 英语自十四世纪起记载 sycomore 指圣经中的无花果；这个词的另一条线常写作 sycamore，逐渐用来指似无花果的悬铃木与槭树。

items.en: Modern English keeps the old fig name for the real fig in Bible lands, while Britain and North America each attach it to a different large tree.
items.cn: 现代英语保留旧名指圣经之地真正的无花果，而英国与北美各自把它安在了不同的大树上。

note.en: Sycamore is checked against look-alike plant names and against the trees it is often confused with.
note.cn: 把 sycamore 与拼写相近的植物名以及常被混淆的树放在一起比较。

entries.definition: an alternative spelling of the same tree name
entries.definitionCN: 同一树名的另一种拼写

entries.definition: a biblical tree name, generally thought to be the black mulberry
entries.definitionCN: 圣经中的树名，一般认为指黑桑；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the hollow fruit cluster of the fig
entries.definitionCN: 无花果的肉质隐头花序果实，与 sykon（无花果）同根

entries.definition: a large tree with flaking bark, called a sycamore in North America
entries.definitionCN: 树皮剥落的大树，在北美就叫 sycamore（悬铃木）

entries.definition: a tree with paired winged seeds that supplies pale timber
entries.definitionCN: 结对生翅果、产浅色木材的树（槭），sycomore 在英国常是其中一种

entries.definition: a tree whose sweet fruit is carried inside a hollow stem
entries.definitionCN: 果实长在中空花托内的甜味果树，即 sycamore 最古老的所指

normalIntro.en: Sycamore is an old Mediterranean plant name that English handed to whatever big tree stood nearby.
normalIntro.cn: sycamore 是个古老的地中海植物名，英语把它一次次安在附近的大树身上。

normal.en: Sycamore maple is the full name of the British tree, and the maple half points to the shape of its leaves.
normal.cn: 英国那种树的完整名称是 sycamore maple，其中 maple 一半正好点出叶子的形状。

normal.en: A sycamore sheds its bark in flakes, so its trunk looks like a patched quilt.
normal.cn: 槭树的树皮成片剥落，树干看上去像一条打补丁的被子。

normal.en: Bible lands keep the fig sense: the scripture tree called by this name is a thick-trunked fig, not a maple.
normal.cn: 圣经之地保留着无花果义：经文里的那棵 sycamore 是树干粗壮的无花果，不是槭树。

normal.en: In the United States a sycamore is a plane tree, so the same word names two different trees across the Atlantic.
normal.cn: 在美国，sycamore 是悬铃木，因此同一个词在大西洋两岸指两种不同的树。

normal.en: Sycamore furniture has a pale, hard, close grain and is used for violins and bowls.
normal.cn: 槭木家具木质浅色坚硬、纹理细密，常用于小提琴与木碗。

abstract.en: Picture one wide crown over a field gate, casting a square of shade where people stop to talk.
abstract.cn: 想象一片宽大的树冠罩在田门上方，投下一块方方的树荫，人们停下来说话。

abstract.en: Imagine rubbing the trunk and feeling the flakes of bark come away under your palm.
abstract.cn: 想象你伸手摸树干，掌心下剥落的树皮一片片掉下来。

abstract.en: Think of a plane tree by an American creek and a maple in a British lane sharing one old name by accident.
abstract.cn: 想一想要么是美洲溪边的悬铃木，要么是英国把小道的槭树，被同一个名字错认在了一起。

examples.en: They sat in the shade of a tall sycamore.
examples.cn: 他们坐在一棵高大槭树的树荫下。

examples.en: The sycamores in our street are old enough to predate the houses.
examples.cn: 我们街上那些槭树比房子还老。

examples.en: The sycamore in the Bible story grew figs as sweet as honey.
examples.cn: 圣经故事里那棵无花果树结的果子甜得像蜂蜜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「西科莫」——西边科片剥落，露出树皮斑驳；只是拆音联想，与词源无关

root: 闪米特语 shiqmah（巴勒斯坦的无花果树）→ 希腊语 sykomoros（民间词源拆作 sykon 无花果 + moron 桑）→ 拉丁语 sycomorus → 古法语 sicamor / sycomore → 英语 sycamore；核心义「果子厚实的古树」，后来漂移到槭树与悬铃木。

sensesIntro.en: Sycamore starts as a fig of Bible lands, then became the English name of a European maple and a North American plane, and finally of landbound landmarks, timber, and place names.
sensesIntro.cn: sycamore 起于圣经之地的无花果，后来成为欧洲槭树与北美悬铃木的英语名，最后又扩展为地标、木材与地名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one big tree by the road, with a broad crown and bark peeling in pale patches.
core.cn: 核心意象：路边一棵大树，树冠很宽，树皮剥落后露出浅色斑块。

branches.en: The British maple takes the old name by custom rather than by descent.
branches.cn: 英国的槭树是按习惯、而非按血统承接了这个旧名。

branches.en: The American plane earns the name by looking like the same ancient tree.
branches.cn: 美国的悬铃木靠长得像那棵古树而得了这个名字。

branches.en: The biblical fig is the oldest and truest owner of the name.
branches.cn: 圣经里的无花果才是这个名字最早、最本真的主人。

branches.en: A single old tree and the place named after it keep the word on the map.
branches.cn: 一棵老树和以它命名的地方，把这个词留在了地图上。

branches.en: The pale hard wood of the maple carries the tree name into the workshop.
branches.cn: 槭树那种浅色坚硬的木材，把树名带进了木工房。

intro.en: Sycamore is a whole borrowed word rather than a formed compound; its pieces come from the Greek spelling that the word came in through.
intro.cn: sycamore 是整体借入的词，并非英语新造的合成词；它的零件来自该词传入时所经的希腊语拼写。

latinIntro.en: Latin sycomorus is a borrowed Greek plant name; older Greek forms of the fig word are reconstructed, so the deeper ending is source uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sycomorus 是借来的希腊语植物名；更早表示无花果的希腊语形式属于重构，更深层的词尾来源不确定。

items.example: Shiqmah is the oldest recorded name behind the plant word.
items.exampleCN: shiqmah 是这个词背后最早有记录的植物名。

items.example: Sykon explains why the word once meant a fig tree.
items.exampleCN: sykon 说明了为什么这个词曾经指无花果树。

items.example: Sykomoros is the Greek form of the plant name.
items.exampleCN: sykomoros 是这个名字的希腊语形式。

items.example: Sycomorus is the Latin form that entered the European languages.
items.exampleCN: sycomorus 是进入欧洲各语言的拉丁语形式。

items.example: The element syco- appears in botanical compounds such as syconium.
items.exampleCN: 语素 syco- 出现在 syconium 这类植物学复合词中。

items.meaning: the final part of the word, explained by folk etymology as mulberry
items.meaningCN: 词的尾段，民间词源解释为「桑」
items.example: The ending -more shows how folk etymology reshaped a borrowed name.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -more 显示了民间词源如何改造一个借来的名字。

items.meaning: a variant spelling of the tree name
items.example: Sycomore keeps the French vowel of the borrowed word.
items.exampleCN: sycomore 保留了借词中的法语元音。

items.meaning: the maple, the plane, or the fig, by region
items.meaningCN: 按地区分别指槭树、悬铃木或无花果
items.example: Sycamore shows how plant names travel between regions.
items.exampleCN: sycamore 展示了植物名在不同地区之间如何游走。

items.example: The suffix -s forms sycamores beside the lane.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -s 构成 sycamores，表示路边的一片槭树。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 无花果（与 sycomorus 释义相通的拉丁植物名）

definition_zh: 音节；一个音节发出的声音；只言片语（一句也不说时说 not a syllable）
definition_en: one unit of pronunciation that contains a vowel sound, often with consonants around it, and that can be said in one breath
core_image: 一行单词被轻轻切开，每一刀落下处就是一个可以一口气说出的音块
scene: 语言老师在黑板上写出一个很长的单词，然后用粉笔在字母之间点了几下。The teacher tapped the blackboard once for every syllable of the long word.
sceneCN: 这里 syllable 指的是「音节」（第 1 个义项：一个可以一口气发出的读音单位）；句意：老师每念这个词的一个音节，就在黑板上敲一下。

pos.zh: 只言片语；一个字（多见于否定句中，表示一句话也没说）

senses.title: A unit of sound you can say in one breath
senses.definition: a single sound group with one vowel, which a word is divided into when spoken
senses.definitionCN: 一个包含元音的读音单位，词在说出时被切成若干个这样的单位
senses.example: The word table has two syllables.
senses.exampleCN: table（桌子）这个词有两个音节。
senses.why: Greek syllables meant a taking together, a bundle of sounds caught in one beat, so the first sense is an indivisible unit heard as one sound.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 syllabē 意为「抓在一起」，是把声音抓成一束的一次节拍，所以第一个义项就是听成一整块、不可再分的读音单位。

senses.title: A syllable as a position for stress or tone
senses.definition: a spot in a word where a stress, pitch, or tone can fall
senses.definitionCN: 词中重音、音高或声调可以落下去的一个位置
senses.example: English often places the stress on the first syllable.
senses.exampleCN: 英语常把重音放在第一个音节上。
senses.why: Once sounds are cut into units, rhythm can be taught by stressing or singing some of them, so a syllable also becomes a slot for stress, pitch, or tone.
senses.whyCN: 声音一旦被切成单位，节奏就能靠重读或唱出其中某些单位来教，于是音节也成了承载重音、音高或声调的位置。

senses.title: A written piece of a word
senses.definition: the letters of a word divided into written groups that match the spoken syllables
senses.definitionCN: 把一个词写成的字母按读音划分成的若干小组
senses.example: The dictionary divides the word into syllables on the line.
senses.exampleCN: 词典在这行里把这个词按音节分开了。
senses.why: When speech is written down, the same cut follows the sounds across letters, giving a written unit that writers use to break a word at the end of a line.
senses.whyCN: 语音一旦被写下，同样的切口就随声音落在字母上，形成书写单位，写作者便用它在行尾断开一个词。

senses.title: The smallest part of an utterance
senses.definition: the smallest separate piece of speech, usually in a negative statement
senses.definitionCN: 言语中最小的一段，多用于否定说法
senses.example: She did not say a syllable about the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 关于这个计划，她一个字也没说。
senses.why: A syllable is measured by how little it holds, so an English idiom asks for even one and gets none: not a syllable means total silence.
senses.whyCN: 音节胜在它最小，所以英语习语连一个音节都不肯放过——not a syllable 就是完全沉默。

senses.title: A step in spelling out aloud
senses.definition: one part spoken at a time when a word is spelled or read out slowly
senses.definitionCN: 把一个词慢慢拼读或念出时，一次读出的一个部分
senses.example: He read the name out syllable by syllable.
senses.exampleCN: 他把那个名字一个音节一个音节地念出来。
senses.why: Say a word unit by unit and anyone can follow it, so a syllable also becomes the pace of slow, careful spelling out aloud.
senses.whyCN: 把一个词一个单位一个单位地说出来，谁都能跟得上，于是音节也成了慢慢、仔细拼读时的节拍。

intro.en: Syllable comes from Latin syllaba, from Greek syllabē, a taking together of letters or sounds.
intro.cn: syllable 来自拉丁语 syllaba，源出希腊语 syllabē，原意是把字母或声音「抓在一起」。

items.en: Syllabē was formed on syllambanein, to take together, from syn, with, and a root for take; the tense vowel later became short in Latin.
items.cn: syllabē 由 syllambanein（抓在一起）构成，前缀 syn 意为「共同」，词根意为「抓取」；这个词后来在拉丁语中元音缩短。

items.en: Grammar taught the term as a sound group made of consonant and vowel, so a syllable became a unit that could be counted.
items.cn: 语法学把这个词讲成由辅音和元音组成的声音群，于是音节成了可以数得清的单位。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word as syllaba, a syllable as a part of speech spoken in one breath.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入希腊语作 syllaba，指说话时一口气发出的一个部分。

items.en: Old French took the Latin noun as sillabe, and English received the early form syllabe from it.
items.cn: 古法语把拉丁名词借作 sillabe，英语又从古法语得到早期的 syllabe。

items.en: English used syllabe for a part of a word heard as one sound, in grammar handbooks of the late Middle Ages.
items.cn: 中古晚期起，英语语法手册用 syllabe 指一个词里听成一整块声音的部分。

items.en: Modern spelling settled as syllable in the sixteenth century, and the word grew a second life as a figure for a tiny piece of speech.
items.cn: 现代拼写在十六世纪定型为 syllable，并表示「极小的言语片段」而有了第二重生命。

note.en: Syllable is compared with its look-alike relatives and with the other terms of pronunciation and spelling.
note.cn: 把 syllable 与形近的同族词，以及发音和拼写领域的其他词放在一起比较。

entries.definition: a set of written signs, each standing for one syllable
entries.definitionCN: 每个符号各代表一个音节的一套文字

entries.definition: a summary or list of a course of study
entries.definitionCN: 课程纲要；教学大纲（是原拼写错的拉丁化，与 syllable 同形不同源）

entries.definition: a form of logical argument with premises and a conclusion
entries.definitionCN: 由前提推结论的逻辑推理；以 syll- 开头，但词根不同

entries.definition: the extra loudness or force given to one part of a word
entries.definitionCN: 重音；重读，落在某个音节上的特别力度

entries.definition: the smallest sound unit that changes meaning
entries.definitionCN: 音位；能区别意义的最小语音单位

entries.definition: the smallest unit that carries meaning
entries.definitionCN: 语素；承载意义的最小单位

normalIntro.en: Syllable, from a Greek verb for taking together, is the sound bundle a speaker picks up as one unit.
normalIntro.cn: syllable 出自希腊语表示「抓在一起」的动词，是说话人当作一个单位抓起来的音块。

normal.en: English grammar keeps the -able adjective apart from the noun, so syllables counts the units of sound.
normal.cn: 英语语法区分 -able 形容词与名词，所以表示「数单位」的是 syllables。

normal.en: The adjective syllabic describes a consonant such as l that can carry a beat on its own.
normal.cn: 形容词 syllabic 描述像 l 这样的辅音，它可以自己扛起一拍。

normal.en: A rhyme is built on the stressed syllable, which is why the final stressed unit is the one that must match.
normal.cn: 押韵建立在重读音节上，所以需要相合的是末尾那个重读单位。

normal.en: Monosyllable joins mono, one, with the same root, and a speaker of monosyllables is a person of few words.
normal.cn: monosyllable 用 mono（一）接同一个词根，而说 monosyllables 的人就是话少的人。

normal.en: Count syllables by clapping: one clap for each beat you hear carries a vowel.
normal.cn: 数音节就拍手：每听到一个带元音的一拍就拍一次手。

abstract.en: Picture a loaf of bread sliced into even pieces; each slice is a syllable of the word.
abstract.cn: 想象一条面包被切成均匀的片，每一片就是词里的一个音节。

abstract.en: Imagine each syllable as a single stone skipped once across a lake.
abstract.cn: 想象每个音节是水面上弹起一次的石头，一块只跳一下。

abstract.en: Think of a syllable as one bead on the string of a bead necklace; string them and you have a word.
abstract.cn: 把一个音节想成串珠项链上的一颗珠子，串起来就是一个词。

examples.en: Please break the word into syllables before you read it aloud.
examples.cn: 朗读之前，请先把这个词分成音节。

examples.en: The first syllable of record is stressed when the word is a noun.
examples.cn: 当 record 用作名词时，重音在第一个音节上。

examples.en: After the argument, they did not speak a syllable to each other.
examples.cn: 争吵之后，他们彼此一个字也没说。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「西劳伯」——老师把词切成一块块，一口一个；只是拆音联想，与词源无关

root: 希腊语 syn（共同）+ 表示抓取的词根 → syllambanein（抓在一起）→ syllabē（音节；朗读时抓在一起的一组字母）→ 拉丁语 syllaba → 古法语 sillabe → 英语 syllable；核心义「一口气抓在一起的一组声音」。

sensesIntro.en: Syllable begins as a sound unit said in one breath, then serves as a place for stress and tone, as a written unit, and finally as a figure for the smallest scrap of speech.
sensesIntro.cn: syllable 起初指一口气说出的一个读音单位，接着成为重音与声调的位置、书写上的单位，最后被用作「极小的言语片段」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a word cut with a knife into sound blocks, each said in one breath.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个词被刀切成若干音块，每一块都能一口气说出。

branches.en: The spoken unit with one vowel is the base sense.
branches.cn: 带一个元音的口语单位是基本义项。

branches.en: Stress and slow spelling out both use the syllable as a beat to lean on.
branches.cn: 重音与慢速拼读都把音节当作可以依靠的一拍。

branches.en: The written split is a second face of the sound split.
branches.cn: 书写上的音节划分是声音划分的第二副面孔。

branches.en: The idiom not a syllable stretches the smallest unit into a measure of silence.
branches.cn: 习语「一个字也不」把这个最小单位拉长为衡量沉默的尺子。

branches.en: Stress falls where a syllable can carry it, which is what makes rhythm.
branches.cn: 重音落在能扛住它的音节上，节奏正是由此产生。

intro.en: Syllable is a noun borrowed whole from Greek and Latin, with syllabic, syllabify, and monosyllable built on it in English.
intro.cn: syllable 是从希腊语、拉丁语整体借入的名词，英语在它基础上造出 syllabic、syllabify 与 monosyllable。

latinIntro.en: Greek syn and the verb syllambanein are the recorded sources; the tense vowel of syllabē became short in Latin syllaba, which is why the modern spelling shows -lla-.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 syn 与动词 syllambanein 是有记录可查的来源；syllabē 的长元音在拉丁语 syllaba 中变短，现代拼写里的 -lla- 正源于此。

items.example: The prefix syn- appears in a shortened form inside syllable.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 syn- 在 syllable 中以缩短的形式出现。

items.example: Syllambanein is the verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: syllambanein 是这个名词背后的动词。

items.example: Syllabē named a group of letters said together.
items.exampleCN: syllabē 指一组被一起念出的字母。

items.example: Syllaba is the shortened Latin form that gave English -lla-.
items.exampleCN: syllaba 是缩短的拉丁形式，英语中的 -lla- 由此而来。

items.meaning: a unit of sound said in one breath
items.meaningCN: 一口气说出的读音单位
items.example: Syllable kept the meaning of the Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: syllable 沿用了拉丁名词的意义。

items.meaningCN: 构成形容词 syllabic 的后缀
items.example: The adjective syllabic is built with the suffix -able, not with -able meaning can be.
items.exampleCN: 形容词 syllabic 里的 -able 是构形后缀，不是「可以被……」那个后缀。

items.example: The suffix -ic turns syllab- into the adjective syllabic.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 把 syllab- 变成形容词 syllabic。

items.example: The suffix -ify forms syllabify, to divide into syllables.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ify 构成 syllabify，表示把词分成音节。

items.example: The prefix mono- gives monosyllable, a word of one syllable.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 mono- 构成 monosyllable，即单音节词。

items.example: The suffix -s forms syllables as in two syllables.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -s 构成 syllables，如 two syllables（两个音节）。

latinEntries.meaning: a list, originally a misreading of Greek sittybas
latinEntries.meaningCN: 清单（拉丁语误抄希腊语 sittybas 而来；与 syllable 同形不同源）

definition_zh: 同情；体谅；赞同；支持（某主张或事业）（英式拼写，美式拼作 sympathize）
definition_en: to feel sorry for someone who is in trouble and show that you understand, or to agree with and support a plan or cause
core_image: 一只手轻轻按在对方手背上：不必多说话，已经站在同一侧
scene: 雨夜的车站里，一位旅客的行李被人撞翻了，旁边有人停下帮他收拾。She sympathised with him over his lost luggage.
sceneCN: 这里 sympathise 指的是「同情」（第 1 个义项：为陷入困境的人感到难过并表达理解）；句意：她对他的行李丢失表示同情。

pos.zh: 同情；体谅（常与 with 连用）
赞同；支持（某种主张、计划或事业）

derivatives.zh: 同情；同情心；赞同（动词与 -y 名词同出希腊语 sympatheia）
同情的；体谅的；赞同的（-ic 形容词）
同情者；支持者（英式拼写）
不同情的；冷淡的（un- 否定 + sympathetic）

senses.title: To feel sorry for someone in trouble
senses.definition: to feel and show that you are sorry someone is unhappy or in difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 对别人难过或陷入困境感到遗憾并表现出来
senses.example: I sympathise with you about losing the job.
senses.exampleCN: 你丢了工作，我深表同情。
senses.why: Greek sym, with, plus pathos, feeling, make the verb say I feel with you, so the first sense is shared sorrow.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 sym（共同）加 pathos（感受），使这个动词的含义就是「与你一同感受」，所以第一义便是分担悲伤的同情。

senses.title: To understand someone s reasons
senses.definition: to understand why someone acted or decided as they did
senses.definitionCN: 理解某人为什么这样行事或这样决定
senses.example: She sympathised with his wanting a quieter life.
senses.exampleCN: 她体谅他想要更安静生活的心思。
senses.why: Sharing a feeling folds into knowing where it came from, so understanding another s reasons is the quiet side of the same shared feeling.
senses.whyCN: 共感一旦折叠进「知道这感受从哪里来」，理解他人的理由就成了共享感受的另一面。

senses.title: To agree with a plan or cause
senses.definition: to agree with and give support to an aim, movement, or decision
senses.definitionCN: 认同并支持某个目标、运动或决定
senses.example: Most residents sympathise with the call for safer roads.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数居民都赞同要求道路更安全的呼声。
senses.why: When two people feel the same way about a cause, sympathy becomes support, and the verb turns from the bedside to the campaign office.
senses.whyCN: 当两个人对同一事业感受一致，同情就变成了支持，这个动词也从病床边搬到了办公室。

senses.title: To make your sorrow known
senses.definition: to tell someone in words that you are sorry about what has happened to them
senses.definitionCN: 用言语告诉某人，你为他遇到的事感到难过
senses.example: We sympathised with the family after the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 火灾之后，我们向这家人表示了同情。
senses.why: A feeling that is felt still needs a voice; the verb also covers the act of speaking the sorrow aloud to those who suffer.
senses.whyCN: 感觉到的东西还需要发出声音，这个动词也覆盖了把难过当众说给受苦者听的那个动作。

senses.title: To be in agreement in general
senses.definition: to share the same view or outlook as another person
senses.definitionCN: 与另一人持有相同的看法或倾向
senses.example: Their tastes in music sympathise with each other.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在音乐上的品味彼此相合。
senses.why: Because sympathy begins with like feeling, an older and wider use of the verb describes any two things that fit together in tune.
senses.whyCN: 既然同情起于「相同的感受」，这个动词更早、更广的一种用法便描述任何彼此合拍、同一调门的两样东西。

intro.en: Sympathise is the English verb of sympathy, which English took from French sympathie, itself from Greek sympatheia, shared feeling.
intro.cn: sympathise 是 sympathy 的英语动词形式，sympathy 由法语 sympathie 而来，而法语又源自希腊语 sympatheia，意为「共同的感受」。

items.en: Sympatheia was formed on syn, with, and pathos, what one experiences, and named the having of a feeling together.
items.cn: sympatheia 由 syn（共同）与 pathos（所经历的感受）构成，指与他人共有一份感受。

items.en: Stoic writers used sympatheia for the mutual tie between parts of the universe, and the idea passed into medicine as an affinity between organs.
items.cn: 斯多葛派用 sympatheia 指宇宙各部分之间的相互关联，这一观念又进入医学，指器官之间的感应。

items.en: Latin took the Greek noun as sympathia, kept as a learned word beside the native verb compati, to suffer with.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入希腊名词作 sympathia，它与本土动词 compati（一同承受）并存，属于书卷式借词。

items.en: French sympathiser was the verb built on sympathie for sharing a feeling, used first of physical affinity and then of human feeling.
items.cn: 法语动词 sympathiser 由 sympathie 构成，最初用于物与物之间的相合，后来才用于人的情感。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the sixteenth century in the sense of agreeing in feeling; the -ise ending follows French.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入该动词，义为「感受上彼此一致」；-ise 词尾沿袭法语拼写。

items.en: Modern English narrows the verb to sharing someone s sorrow and supporting a cause, while British and American practice split the spelling into sympathise and sympathize.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个动词收窄为分担他人悲伤与支持某项事业，而英式与美式惯例把拼写分成 sympathise 与 sympathize 两种。

note.en: Sympathise is compared with its spelling siblings and with the nearby verbs for feeling sorry, understanding, and agreeing.
note.cn: 把 sympathise 与同族的拼写变体，以及表示难过、理解和同意的邻近动词放在一起对比。

entries.definition: the American spelling of the same verb
entries.definitionCN: 同一动词的美式拼写（-ize 对应英式 -ise）

entries.definition: shared sorrow or support
entries.definitionCN: 同情；同情心；赞同（sympathise 的名词形）

entries.definition: showing or caused by sympathy
entries.definitionCN: 表示同情的；体谅的（-ic 形容词）

entries.definition: a sign that stands for an idea
entries.definitionCN: 符号；只是 sym- 开头相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to feel sorry for someone
entries.definitionCN: 怜悯；觉得某人可怜（比 sympathise 多一分居高临下的意味）

entries.definition: to comfort someone in sorrow
entries.definitionCN: 安慰；抚慰（强调行动上的安抚）

entries.definition: to express sorrow together with someone
entries.definitionCN: 同情；共同表示难过（正式用语）

entries.definition: to share and understand another person s feelings
entries.definitionCN: 共情；设身处地理解他人的感受

normalIntro.en: Sympathise takes sym, together, and path-, feeling: to feel together is the heart of every sense.
normalIntro.cn: sympathise 由 sym（共同）与 path-（感受）组成：一同感受，贯穿它的每一个义项。

normal.en: The -ise ending is British; American spelling writes the verb as sympathize.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ise 是英式拼法，美式写作 sympathize。

normal.en: The object needs the preposition with, as in sympathise with a friend.
normal.cn: 这个动词后面要接介词 with，如 sympathise with a friend。

normal.en: The same root -path- appears in pathetic, apathy, and empathy, all to do with feeling.
normal.cn: 同一个词根 -path- 也出现在 pathetic、apathy、empathy 里，全都与感受有关。

normal.en: Sympathy came first and the verb was built on it, so the noun names the feeling and the verb names the act.
normal.cn: 名词 sympathy 先出现，动词由它构成，所以名词指那份感受，动词指表达感受的动作。

normal.en: Unlike pity, to sympathise with someone treats the person as an equal, standing beside them rather than above.
normal.cn: 与 pity 不同，sympathise with 某人把对方当平等的人，是站在旁边而不是站在上方。

abstract.en: Picture two hands resting on the same table, one trembling and one steady over it.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手搁在同一张桌上，一只在发抖，另一只稳稳地覆在它上面。

abstract.en: Imagine a fever chart where two lines move up and down in the same rhythm.
abstract.cn: 想象一张体温曲线图，两条线按同样的节奏一起上升、一起下落。

abstract.en: Think of hearing the word path in the middle and walking a mile in the other person s shoes.
abstract.cn: 留意词中间那截 path（路），想象你沿着对方的路走了一英里。

examples.en: We all sympathise with the families who lost their homes.
examples.cn: 我们都同情那些失去家园的家庭。

examples.en: Although he sympathised with the workers, he could not join the strike.
examples.cn: 尽管他同情工人们的处境，却无法参加罢工。

examples.en: She has always sympathised with his reasons for moving abroad.
examples.cn: 她一直体谅他移居海外的理由。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「辛怕theta」——你受苦，我也替你担心；只是拆音联想，与词源无关

root: 希腊语 syn（共同）+ pathos（所经历的感受）→ sympatheia（共感；宇宙与器官间的感应）→ 拉丁语 sympathia → 法语 sympathie 与其动词 sympathiser → 英语 sympathise；核心义「与他人的感受合为一处」。

sensesIntro.en: Sympathise moves from sharing a person s sorrow, to understanding their reasons, to supporting a cause, to saying the sorrow aloud, and at last to any two things agreeing in tune.
sensesIntro.cn: sympathise 从分担他人的悲伤，走向理解对方的理由，再到支持某项事业、把难过说出口，最后广及任何两样东西的彼此合拍。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand laid over a trembling hand, saying nothing but sharing the same feeling.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手覆在发抖的手上，不出声，却共有同一份感受。

branches.en: Feeling sorry for someone and saying so are the spoken and silent faces of the same sense.
branches.cn: 替人难过与把难过说出来，是同一义项的无声与有声两面。

branches.en: Understanding reasons is shared feeling turned toward the mind.
branches.cn: 理解理由，是共享感受转向头脑的那一边。

branches.en: Supporting a cause is shared feeling turned into a public stance.
branches.cn: 支持事业，是共享感受化成了公开的立场。

branches.en: The widest sense keeps only the idea of two things agreeing in tune.
branches.cn: 最宽的义项只留下两样东西彼此合拍这一点。

branches.en: All three senses stand on the ancient pair syn and pathos, together and feeling.
branches.cn: 这三个义项都立在 syn 与 pathos 这一对古老成分上，即「共同」与「感受」。

intro.en: Sympathise is built from the Greek elements syn and pathos plus the verb ending -ise, and the same pieces make sympathy, sympathetic, and unsympathetic.
intro.cn: sympathise 由希腊语成分 syn 与 pathos 加上动词词尾 -ise 构成，同样的零件也造出 sympathy、sympathetic 与 unsympathetic。

latinIntro.en: Sympatheia and pathos are recorded Greek words; Latin kept sympathia as a learned borrowing rather than a native word.
latinIntro.cn: sympatheia 与 pathos 都是有记录的希腊语词；拉丁语把 sympathia 作为书卷借词保留，并非本土词。

items.example: The prefix syn- becomes sym- before p in sympathise.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 syn- 在 sympathise 中位于 p 前，变为 sym-。

items.meaningCN: 所经历的事；所承受的感受
items.example: Pathos is the feeling element behind the verb.
items.exampleCN: pathos 是这个动词背后的「感受」成分。

items.example: Sympatheia put together the prefix and the feeling noun.
items.exampleCN: sympatheia 把共同前缀与感受名词合在一起。

items.example: Sympathia was the Latin learned form, beside the native compati.
items.exampleCN: sympathia 是拉丁语的书卷借词形式，与本土的 compati 并存。

items.example: French sympathiser is the immediate verb source.
items.exampleCN: 法语 sympathiser 是直接的动词来源。

items.meaningCN: 构成动词的词尾，英式拼写为主
items.example: The suffix -ise spells the verb in British usage, against -ize in American usage.
items.exampleCN: 英式用法以词尾 -ise 拼写这个词，美式则用 -ize。

items.meaningCN: 过去式与过去分词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ed forms sympathised for the past tense.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成过去式 sympathised。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms sympathising, as in a sympathising smile.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 sympathising，如「带着同情的微笑」。

items.example: The suffix -y makes the noun sympathy from the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 由同一词干造出名词 sympathy。

items.example: The suffix -ic makes the adjective sympathetic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成形容词 sympathetic。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 共同的感受；天然的相合

definition_zh: 交响乐；交响曲；交响乐团；和谐；协调一致
definition_en: a long piece of music for a large orchestra, or a pleasing combination of sounds or things that work well together
core_image: 许多把乐器同时发声，汇成一片整齐流动的声浪
scene: 演出结束后，整座音乐厅都站起来鼓掌。After the concert ended, the whole hall stood up and cheered for the symphony.
sceneCN: 这里 symphony 是「交响曲」（第 1 个义项：供管弦乐团演奏的大型乐曲）；句意：演出结束后，整座音乐厅都站起来为这首交响曲鼓掌。

derivatives.zh: 由 symphony 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为「交响乐的；交响曲的」
由 symphonic 加副词后缀 -ally 构成，义为「以交响乐的方式」
由 symphony 加表人后缀 -ist 构成，义为「交响曲作曲家」
共用希腊语词根 philein，义为「爱乐的；交响乐团的」

senses.title: A large orchestral work
senses.definition: a long piece of music in several movements, written for a full orchestra
senses.definitionCN: 为大型管弦乐团创作、通常含几个乐章的长篇乐曲
senses.example: The orchestra played a symphony by Beethoven.
senses.exampleCN: 乐团演奏了一部贝多芬的交响曲。
senses.why: Greek syn- means together and phone means sound, so a symphony was literally a sounding together of many instruments.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语前缀 syn- 表示「一起」，phone 表示「声音」，symphony 本义就是许多乐器「一起发声」，因此可直接指为整支乐团写成的乐曲。

senses.title: A harmony of sounds
senses.definition: a combination of sounds that is pleasing and well balanced
senses.definitionCN: 悦耳而均衡的组合声音
senses.example: The birds made a symphony of sound at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明时分，鸟儿们奏出一片和声。
senses.why: Since sounding together can also mean sounding pleasantly, the same word names any harmony of sound, not only orchestral music.
senses.whyCN: 「一起发声」也可以意味着「发得悦耳」，所以同一个词也能指任何悦耳和谐的声音，而不限于管弦乐曲。

senses.title: A harmonious mixture
senses.definition: a harmonious mixture of colours, flavours, or activities working together
senses.definitionCN: 颜色、味道或活动彼此协调、融合成一体的组合
senses.example: The garden was a symphony of colour in autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 秋天的花园是色彩的交响。
senses.why: The idea of many parts sounding together easily spreads from hearing to seeing and doing, giving a figurative sense of harmonious mixture.
senses.whyCN: 「许多部分一起发声」的想法很容易从听觉扩展到视觉与行动，于是产生「和谐组合」这一比喻义。

senses.title: A full orchestra
senses.definition: a large orchestra that performs classical music
senses.definitionCN: 演奏古典音乐的大型管弦乐团
senses.example: She has played in the city symphony for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 她在市交响乐团演奏了十年。
senses.why: Because symphonies are the signature works of these groups, English lets the word name the group itself, especially in American usage.
senses.whyCN: 交响曲正是这类团体的招牌曲目，于是英语让这个词直接指这些乐团本身，美式用法尤多。

senses.title: Agreement in action
senses.definition: a state in which several people or parts act in agreement
senses.definitionCN: 多人或多个部分协同一致的状态
senses.example: The two teams worked in symphony on the project.
senses.exampleCN: 两个团队在这个项目上协调一致地合作。
senses.why: If instruments can sound together in tune, people can also act together in tune, so the word reaches the abstract sense of agreement.
senses.whyCN: 既然乐器能合调一起发声，人也能合拍一起行动，于是这个词延伸到「协调一致」这一抽象义。

intro.en: Symphony comes through Latin and Old French from Greek symphonia, a sounding together, built from syn, together, and phone, sound.
intro.cn: symphony 经拉丁语与古法语来自希腊语 symphonia（一起发声），由 syn（一起）与 phone（声音）构成。

items.en: Symphonia means a sounding together and also agreement or concord.
items.cn: symphonia 意为一起发声，也表示一致、和睦。

items.en: Latin takes symphonia as a name for concord and for a kind of music.
items.cn: 拉丁语借用 symphonia，既指和谐一致，也指某种音乐。

items.en: Symphonie reaches French with the general sense of harmony.
items.cn: 古法语 symphonie 以「和谐」的一般含义进入法语。

items.en: Early English uses symphony first for concord and sweet sound.
items.cn: 早期英语的 symphony 先指和谐与悦耳之声。

items.en: Italian usage helps the word settle on a work for orchestra.
items.cn: 在意大利语的推动下，这个词逐渐定指管弦乐曲。

items.en: Modern English extends it to a pleasing mixture of anything.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到任何悦耳和谐的混合。

note.en: Symphony shares its Greek root syn- with many words of togetherness, and sits beside orchestra and concert terms.
note.cn: symphony 与许多表示「共同」的词共享希腊语 syn-，在词义上又与乐团、音乐会一类词相邻。

entries.definitionCN: 交响乐的

entries.definition: a composer of symphonies
entries.definitionCN: 交响曲作曲家

entries.definition: the Greek word for a sounding together
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语「一起发声」，是词源上源

entries.definition: sound or voice
entries.definitionCN: 声音；嗓音，与 symphony 共享 phone 词根

entries.definition: a large group of musicians playing together
entries.definitionCN: 管弦乐团

entries.definition: a piece of music for one soloist and orchestra

entries.definitionCN: 和声；和谐

normalIntro.en: Symphony holds syn, together, and phone, sound: many musicians sounding at once.
normalIntro.cn: symphony 里藏着 syn（一起）与 phone（声音）：许多乐手同时发声。

normal.en: Syn- appears in synchronise, where things occur at the same time.
normal.cn: syn- 也出现在 synchronise 中，表示事情同时发生。

normal.en: The -phony part links to phonetics, the study of speech sounds.
normal.cn: 词中的 -phony 与 phonetics（语音学）相连，都与声音有关。

normal.en: A symphony orchestra is the large group that plays symphonies.
normal.cn: a symphony orchestra 就是演奏交响曲的大型乐团。

normal.en: The plural symphonies keeps one -y and adds -ies.
normal.cn: 复数 symphonies 是把词尾 -y 变成 -ies。

normal.en: The phrase a symphony of colours borrows the harmony of sound.
normal.cn: a symphony of colours 借用了声音的和谐感。

abstract.en: Picture an empty hall before the conductor lifts the baton.
abstract.cn: 想象指挥举起指挥棒之前，空荡荡的音乐厅。

abstract.en: Hear one violin, then the whole orchestra joining in.
abstract.cn: 先听见一把小提琴，再听见整个乐团一起加入。

abstract.en: See autumn leaves in red and gold blending into one scene.
abstract.cn: 看着红与金黄的秋叶融成一片风景。

examples.en: Mozart wrote his first symphony before he was ten.
examples.cn: 莫扎特不到十岁就写下了第一部交响曲。

examples.en: The festival ends with a late symphony by Mahler.
examples.cn: 音乐节以马勒的一部晚间交响曲收尾。

examples.en: Lights from the harbour formed a symphony of reflections on the water.
examples.cn: 港口的灯光在水面上交织成一片倒影的交响。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「心符你」——乐手们按总谱同声齐奏，心跟着符音，就是一起发声的交响；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 syn-（一起）+ phone（声音）→ symphonia（一起发声；和谐）→ 拉丁语 symphonia → 古法语 symphonie → 英语 symphony，核心义「许多声音合在一起」。

sensesIntro.en: Symphony begins with the orchestral work, keeps the older sense of pleasant harmony, then widens to mixtures, the orchestra itself, and agreement.
sensesIntro.cn: symphony 从管弦乐曲义出发，保留「悦耳和谐」的旧义，再扩展到和谐组合、乐团本身与协调一致。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many instruments sounding at the same time.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多乐器同时发声。

branches.en: The orchestral work is the dominant modern sense.
branches.cn: 管弦乐曲是现代最主要的义项。

branches.en: Pleasant sounding together is the older harmony sense.
branches.cn: 悦耳地一起发声是较早的和谐义。

branches.en: Both mixture and agreement extend the idea of parts in tune.
branches.cn: 和谐组合与协调一致都延伸了各部分合拍的想法。

branches.en: A symphony is also judged by how its voices blend.
branches.cn: 交响曲也常以各声部融合得好不好来评价。

branches.en: The orchestra and its signature work often share one name.
branches.cn: 乐团与它的招牌曲目常常共用一个名称。

intro.en: Symphony is built from the Greek prefix syn-, meaning together, and the root phone, meaning sound.
intro.cn: symphony 由希腊语前缀 syn-（一起）与词根 phone（声音）构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed Greek symphonia while keeping the sense of concord and agreement.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语借入希腊语 symphonia，同时保留了和谐与一致的含义。

items.exampleCN: 前缀 syn- 出现在许多英语词的开头。

items.meaning: to make things happen at the same time

items.exampleCN: synchronise 保留了「时间上一起」的想法。

items.example: Symphony is the whole noun.
items.exampleCN: symphony 是整个名词。

items.meaning: a form for names of things
items.meaningCN: 名词词尾，标示事物名称
items.example: The ending -y closes the borrowed word.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 收束这个借来的词。

items.example: Phone appears in phonetics and telephone.
items.exampleCN: phone 出现在 phonetics 与 telephone 中。

items.example: Phonetics shows the sound root clearly.
items.exampleCN: phonetics 清楚显示了「声音」词根。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms symphonic.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 构成 symphonic。

items.example: Symphonic describes music in that style.
items.exampleCN: symphonic 描述那种风格的音乐。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms symphonist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 构成 symphonist。

items.example: Symphonist names the person.
items.exampleCN: symphonist 指人。

definition_zh: 专题研讨会；学术讨论会；专题论文集
definition_en: a meeting where experts give talks and discuss one subject, or a published collection of such talks
core_image: 一群学者围坐长桌，轮流举杯发言，各出高见
scene: 来自几所大学的学者聚在一起，就同一主题轮流发言讨论。Scholars from several universities gathered at the annual symposium to discuss water resources.
sceneCN: 这里 symposium 是「专题研讨会」（第 1 个义项：专家就同一主题发言讨论的会议）；句意：几所大学的学者聚集在一年一度的研讨会上讨论水资源问题。

pos.zh: 专题研讨会；学术讨论会

collocations.zh: 在一场关于气候的研讨会上

derivatives.zh: 由 symposium 加表人后缀 -ast 构成，义为「研讨会参加者；古代酒宴宾客」
由 symposium 加后缀 -ac 构成，义为「研讨会性的；酒宴的」
由 symposium 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「研讨会的」

senses.title: An academic meeting
senses.titleCN: 专题研讨会；学术讨论会
senses.definition: a formal meeting at which experts give short talks and discuss one topic
senses.definitionCN: 专家发表简短报告并讨论同一主题的正式会议
senses.example: She presented her research at a symposium on genetics.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一场遗传学研讨会上报告了自己的研究。
senses.why: Greek symposion meant a drinking together, so the idea of a group gathering to exchange words naturally became a meeting for discussion.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 symposion 本义是「一起饮酒」，因此「一群人聚在一起交谈」很自然就演变成讨论同一主题的会议。

senses.title: A printed collection
senses.definition: a collection of articles or papers on one subject, often published after a meeting
senses.definitionCN: 围绕同一主题的文章或论文汇编，常在会议之后出版
senses.example: The papers were published as a symposium on urban history.
senses.exampleCN: 这些论文以城市史专题论文集的形式出版了。
senses.why: Because the talks of such a meeting are often printed together, the word moves from the event to the volume that records it.
senses.whyCN: 会上发言常常结集付印，所以这个词从「活动」转指「记录活动的文集」。

senses.title: The ancient drinking party
senses.definition: in ancient Greece, a drinking party after a meal, often with talk, music, and debate
senses.definitionCN: 古希腊饭后举行的酒宴，常伴谈话、音乐与辩论
senses.example: Plato set a famous dialogue at a symposium.
senses.exampleCN: 柏拉图把一部著名的对话设在一次酒宴上。
senses.why: This is the original sense of the Greek word, kept alive in classical studies of Greek social life.
senses.whyCN: 这是希腊语原本的含义，在古典学术对希腊社交生活的研究中一直沿用。

senses.title: A lively gathering
senses.definition: a cheerful social gathering with food, drink, and long conversation
senses.definitionCN: 伴有饮食与长谈的愉快社交聚会
senses.example: The evening turned into a symposium of old friends.
senses.exampleCN: 那个夜晚变成了一场老友的欢聚畅谈。
senses.why: The ancient sense of guests drinking and talking still survives when writers use the word for a convivial party.
senses.whyCN: 古代「宾客饮酒交谈」的含义仍存，作家用它来形容亲切热闹的聚会时正是取这一层。

senses.title: An exchange of views
senses.definition: an occasion or activity marked by free, serious exchange of opinions
senses.definitionCN: 以自由而认真地交换观点为特征的活动或场合
senses.example: The debate became a symposium on the meaning of justice.
senses.exampleCN: 那场辩论变成了一次关于正义含义的思辨讨论。
senses.why: The core idea of talking together rather than a fixed event carries the word into any serious exchange of views.
senses.whyCN: 核心想法是「一起交谈」而不是某个固定活动，这使这个词可以指任何严肃的意见交换。

intro.en: Symposium comes through Latin from Greek symposion, a drinking together, from syn, together, and posis, a drinking.
intro.cn: symposium 经拉丁语来自希腊语 symposion（一起饮酒），由 syn（一起）与 posis（饮）构成。

items.en: Symposion means a drinking party and the talk that goes with it.
items.cn: symposion 意为饮酒聚会以及随之而来的谈论。

items.en: Greek writers use it for learned conversation and for written dialogue.
items.cn: 希腊作家用它指博雅清谈，也指写成文字的对话。

items.en: Latin symposium keeps the party sense and the sense of a dialogue.
items.cn: 拉丁语 symposium 保留聚会义与对话义。

items.en: English revives the word for a convivial meeting and for a Platonic dialogue.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语复兴此词，指亲切的聚会与柏拉图式对话。

items.en: The word shifts towards serious discussion and conference use.
items.cn: 这个词转向严肃讨论与会议用法。

items.en: Modern usage restricts it to academic meetings and their papers.
items.cn: 现代用法把它限定为学术会议及其论文集。

note.en: Symposium shares the prefix syn- with many words of togetherness, and sits beside conference and seminar in meaning.
note.cn: symposium 与许多表示「共同」的词共享前缀 syn-，在词义上与会议、研讨课一类词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Symposium hides syn, together, and the drinking root posis: people sitting together to talk.

normal.en: Syn- also starts synchronise and synonym, both about things joined.

normal.en: The plural symposia keeps the Greek ending -a.

normal.en: An academic symposium sounds close to conference but is smaller and more focused.

normal.en: The word keeps a trace of a shared meal behind the shared talk.

abstract.en: Picture a long table with scholars taking turns to speak.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，学者们轮流发言。

abstract.en: Imagine Greek guests sharing wine and arguing about love.
abstract.cn: 想象希腊宾客共饮葡萄酒，争论着爱的问题。

abstract.en: See a printed book of papers stacked after the meeting.
abstract.cn: 想象会议结束后摆成一叠的论文汇编。

examples.en: The department held a symposium on renewable energy.
examples.cn: 该系举办了一场关于可再生能源的研讨会。

examples.en: Papers from the symposia were printed in two volumes.
examples.cn: 这些研讨会的论文分两卷印行。

examples.en: He met his future co author at a symposium in Vienna.
examples.cn: 他在维也纳的一次研讨会上遇到了未来的合著者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「辛波西姆」——专家们辛苦地一波波西来相会，围桌研讨某一专题；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 syn-（一起）+ posis（饮）→ symposion（共饮；宴谈）→ 拉丁语 symposium → 英语 symposium，核心义「聚在一起边谈边议」。

sensesIntro.en: Symposium starts with the academic meeting, then its published papers, and behind both the old party sense of talking and drinking together.
sensesIntro.cn: symposium 以学术研讨会为核心，其次指会后的论文集，而背后是古代「聚会共饮清谈」的旧义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: guests seated together, talking over wine.
core.cn: 核心意象：宾客围坐，边饮边谈。

branches.en: The academic meeting is the standard modern sense.
branches.cn: 学术研讨会是现代标准义项。

branches.en: The papers of the meeting become a collection.
branches.cn: 会议论文结集成册。

branches.en: The ancient party and lively gathering keep the original sense.
branches.cn: 古代酒宴与欢聚保留了原初义。

branches.en: Both a meeting and a free debate centre on exchanging views.
branches.cn: 研讨会与自由辩论都以交换意见为中心。

branches.en: A meeting and its printed papers often share one title.
branches.cn: 会议与其论文集常共用一个名称。

intro.en: Symposium joins the Greek prefix syn-, together, to the root posis, a drinking.
intro.cn: symposium 把希腊语前缀 syn-（一起）与词根 posis（饮）结合在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed Greek symposion as symposium and kept both the banquet and the dialogue senses.

同步；同时发生；协调一致

senses.title: Make things happen at the same time
senses.definition: to make two or more actions, events, or processes happen at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 使两个或更多的动作、事件或过程在同一时间发生
senses.example: The film makes the music synchronise with each step.
senses.exampleCN: 影片让音乐与每一个舞步同步。
senses.why: Greek syn- means together and khronos means time, so the verb literally means to bring things into the same time.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 syn- 表示「一起」，khronos 表示「时间」，所以这个动词字面上就是「把事物放进同一个时间」，这正是第 1 个义项的来源。

senses.title: Set clocks to the same time
senses.definition: to set two or more clocks or watches so that they show the same time
senses.definitionCN: 把两只或更多钟表调到显示同一时间
senses.example: They synchronise their watches before every race.
senses.exampleCN: 每次比赛前他们都会对表。
senses.why: Clocks are the most concrete carriers of time, so making things share a time first becomes a picture of setting timepieces together.
senses.whyCN: 钟表是「时间」最具体的载体，所以让事物共享同一时间，首先落到「把计时器调齐」这一画面。

senses.title: Keep data in step
senses.definition: to make files or data on different devices identical by copying changes between them
senses.definitionCN: 在不同设备之间复制改动，使文件或数据保持一致
senses.example: The app synchronises your notes across all devices.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用会在你所有设备之间同步笔记。
senses.why: Digital tools need copies to be updated at the same moment, so the idea of shared time is borrowed for keeping data in step.
senses.whyCN: 电子工具需要各处副本在同一时刻得到更新，于是「共享时间」的想法被借用来表示数据步调一致。

senses.title: Move in rhythm together
senses.definition: to move or perform at the same speed and rhythm as another person or group
senses.definitionCN: 与他人或团体以相同的速度与节奏移动或表演
senses.example: The swimmers synchronise their strokes as they turn.
senses.exampleCN: 游泳选手在转身时把划水动作调整得同步。
senses.why: Shared timing can be seen as well as measured, so the word also covers movements that stay exactly in step.
senses.whyCN: 共享时间不只可以测量，也可以看见，所以这个词也涵盖始终步调一致的动作。

senses.title: Bring plans into step
senses.definition: to arrange activities or plans so that they work well together
senses.definitionCN: 安排活动或计划，使其相互配合、顺畅衔接
senses.example: Departments synchronise their holidays to avoid gaps.
senses.exampleCN: 各部门把假期安排得协调一致，以免出现空档。
senses.why: When people share timetables their plans fit together, so shared time widens into the abstract sense of coordination.
senses.whyCN: 人们共用时间表时，计划就会彼此吻合，于是「共享时间」扩展为「协调一致」这一抽象义。

intro.en: Synchronise is built on Greek roots: syn, together, and khronos, time, with the English verb ending -ise.
intro.cn: synchronise 建立在希腊语词根之上：syn（一起）与 khronos（时间），再加上英语动词词尾 -ise。

items.en: Syn means together and khronos means time.
items.cn: syn 意为一起，khronos 意为时间。

items.en: Greek builds words such as synchronos, happening at the same time.
items.cn: 希腊语据此构成 synchronos 等词，意为同时发生的。

items.en: Latin science writing takes up the Greek roots in borrowed form.
items.cn: 拉丁语的科学写作以借用形式吸收这些希腊词根。

items.en: Synchronous enters English as a learned term about time.
items.cn: 十七世纪 synchronous 作为关于时间的学术词进入英语。

items.en: Synchronise appears as a verb of clocks, machines, and telegraphy.
items.cn: 十九世纪 synchronise 出现，用于钟表、机器与电报。

items.en: Film, computing, and teamwork widen it to sound, data, and plans.
items.cn: 电影、计算机与协作使用把它扩展到声音、数据与计划。

note.en: Synchronise shares the prefix syn- with many words of togetherness, and sits beside align and coordinate in meaning.
note.cn: synchronise 与许多表示「共同」的词共享前缀 syn-，在词义上与对齐、协调一类词相邻。

entries.definition: the American spelling of the same verb
entries.definitionCN: 同一动词的美式拼写，词义完全相同

entries.definition: the act of making things happen together
entries.definitionCN: 同步；同步化

entries.definition: happening at the same time
entries.definitionCN: 同时发生的；同步的

entries.definition: lasting a long time
entries.definitionCN: 长期的，与 synchronise 共享时间词根 khronos

entries.definition: to bring things into a straight line or agreement
entries.definitionCN: 使成一线；使一致

entries.definition: to make different parts work well together
entries.definitionCN: 协调；使配合

entries.definition: to adjust an instrument against a standard
entries.definitionCN: 校准；标定

normalIntro.en: Synchronise says syn, together, plus khronos, time: to put things into one shared time.
normalIntro.cn: synchronise 由 syn（一起）与 khronos（时间）组成：把事物放进同一段时间。

normal.en: Chronic also carries khronos, the root for time.
normal.cn: chronic（慢性的、长期的）同样含 khronos 这个「时间」词根。

normal.en: British spelling keeps -ise while American spelling uses -ize.
normal.cn: 英式拼写为 synchronise，美式拼写为 synchronize。

normal.en: The noun synchronisation turns the verb into a process.
normal.cn: 名词 synchronisation 把这个动词变成过程名称。

normal.en: Phones synchronise contacts across several devices.
normal.cn: 手机会在多台设备之间同步联系人。

normal.en: The adjective synchronous is the plain state word, without an action.
normal.cn: 形容词 synchronous 表示只描述状态的「同时的」，不含动作。

abstract.en: Watch two second hands click over at once.
abstract.cn: 看着两根秒针同时跳向下一格。

abstract.en: Hear footsteps of a marching band falling on one beat.
abstract.cn: 听着行进的乐队脚步落在同一个鼓点上。

abstract.en: See a film scene where a door slam fits the music exactly.
abstract.cn: 想象电影里关门声恰好卡在音乐的点上。

examples.en: Crews must synchronise their clocks before the launch.
examples.cn: 发射前各机组必须把钟表校准到同一时间。

examples.en: Her breathing synchronised with the rhythm of the rowers.
examples.cn: 她的呼吸与划桨的节奏同步了。

examples.en: The two companies will synchronise the launch of their products.
examples.cn: 两家公司将协调一致地推出各自的产品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「辛克郎」——时钟敲响，辛劳的少年郎一拍一动，全部踩在同一个点上；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 syn-（一起）+ khronos（时间）→ synchronos（同时的）→ 英语 synchronous → synchronize / synchronise，核心义「把事物放进同一时间」。

sensesIntro.en: Synchronise begins with the general act of putting events into one time, then narrows to clocks, data, movement, and finally to plans working together.
sensesIntro.cn: synchronise 先指把事件放进同一时间的通用动作，再依次具体化为对表、数据同步、动作合拍，最后指计划协调一致。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands pointing to the same mark at the same instant.
core.cn: 核心意象：两根指针在同一瞬间指向同一刻度。

branches.en: Shared timing is the general core sense.
branches.cn: 共享时间是最核心的通用义项。

branches.en: Clocks give the most concrete form of that sharing.
branches.cn: 钟表是这种共享最具体的形态。

branches.en: Data and movement are both kept in step by timing.
branches.cn: 数据与动作都靠时间上的一致来保持同步。

branches.en: Coordination is the abstract planning sense.
branches.cn: 协调是抽象的计划义。

branches.en: Both events and files must update at the same moment to stay in step.
branches.cn: 事件与文件都必须同时更新才能步调一致。

intro.en: Synchronise combines the Greek prefix syn-, together, the root khronos, time, and the verb ending -ise.
intro.cn: synchronise 结合了希腊语前缀 syn-（一起）、词根 khronos（时间）与动词词尾 -ise。

latinIntro.en: Classical Latin science prose borrowed Greek chronos, so these elements entered English through Latin in borrowed form.
latinIntro.cn: 古典拉丁语的科学散文借用了希腊语 chronos，这些成分以借用形式经拉丁语进入英语。

items.example: The prefix syn- also starts synonym.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 syn- 也出现在 synonym 中。

items.meaningCN: 一起（在 p、b 前变体）
items.example: Sym- appears in symposium.
items.exampleCN: sym- 出现在 symposium 中。

items.example: The root chron- shows time in chronology.
items.exampleCN: 词根 chron- 在 chronology 中表示时间。

items.meaning: the order of events in time
items.example: Chronology shows the time root plainly.
items.exampleCN: chronology 清楚展示了「时间」词根。

items.example: The ending -ise is the British form.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ise 是英式写法。

items.example: The ending -ize appears in synchronize.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ize 出现在 synchronize 中。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms synchronisation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 synchronisation。

items.meaning: the act of making things happen together
items.example: Synchronisation names the process.
items.exampleCN: synchronisation 指这一过程。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms synchronous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 synchronous。

items.example: Synchronous is the state form.
items.exampleCN: synchronous 是状态形式。

definition_zh: 同义词；近义词；代名词；等义词
definition_en: a word or phrase that has the same or almost the same meaning as another word or phrase in the same language
core_image: 两枚形状不同的钥匙，却能开同一把锁
scene: 备考时，学生把「大」和「巨大」写在同一行，标注为同义关系。In the exam notes, the student wrote big and enormous on the same line and marked them as a synonym pair.
sceneCN: 这里 synonym 是「同义词」（第 1 个义项：与另一个词意义相同或几乎相同的词）；句意：在考试笔记里，学生把「big」和「enormous」写在同一行，并把它们标成一对同义词。

derivatives.zh: 由 synonym 去尾加 -ous 构成，义为「同义的；意义相同的」
由 synonym 加名词后缀 -y 构成，义为「同义关系」
由 synonymous 加 -ly 构成，义为「同义地」

senses.title: A word meaning the same
senses.definition: a word that has the same or nearly the same meaning as another word
senses.definitionCN: 与另一个词意义相同或几乎相同的词
senses.example: The teacher jotted a synonym for each difficult word in the margin.
senses.exampleCN: 老师在页边给每个难词都写下了一个同义词。
senses.why: Greek syn means together and onoma means name, so a synonym is a word that shares a name with another.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 syn 意为「一起」，onoma 意为「名字」，所以同义词就是与另一个词共用一个名字的词。

senses.title: A near word
senses.definition: a word that is very close in meaning rather than exactly identical
senses.definitionCN: 意义非常接近、但并不完全相同的词
senses.example: Many teachers call nearly identical words near synonyms instead of exact ones.
senses.exampleCN: 许多老师把意义极接近的词称为近义词，而不叫完全同义词。
senses.why: Because the Greek element syn only says shared, the word can stretch to mean similar rather than exactly identical.
senses.whyCN: 因为希腊语成分 syn 只表示「共同」，所以这个词也可以放宽为「相近」，而不必完全相同。

senses.title: A byword
senses.definition: a word used as another name for something because it is characteristically associated with it
senses.definitionCN: 因与某事物有典型联系而被用来指代它的另一个名称
senses.example: The region has become a synonym for hospitality in travel guides.
senses.exampleCN: 在旅游指南里，这个地区已经成了热情好客的代名词。
senses.why: When two words are exchanged so often that one stands for the other, the label becomes a byword.
senses.whyCN: 当两个词经常被互换使用、以致一个词可以代表另一个词时，这个词就成了代名词。

senses.title: A scientific alternate name
senses.definition: one of two or more different scientific names applied to the same species
senses.definitionCN: 指同一物种的两个或多个不同学名中的一个
senses.example: Botanists rejected the older synonym and kept the accepted name.
senses.exampleCN: 植物学家舍弃了较早的同名，保留了被接受的那个名称。
senses.why: Taxonomy borrows the word because two labels stand for one organism, an exact parallel of two words for one meaning.
senses.whyCN: 分类学借用这个词，是因为两个名称指同一个生物体，正好对应「两个词指同一个意思」。

intro.en: Synonym joins Greek syn, meaning together, with onoma, meaning name; the pair passed through Latin synonymum and Latin-influenced French into English.
intro.cn: synonym 由希腊语 syn（一起）与 onoma（名字）组合而成，经拉丁语 synonymum 和受拉丁语影响的法语进入英语。

items.en: Synonymos means having the same name, from syn together and onoma name.
items.cn: 希腊语 synonymos 意为「同名的」，由 syn（一起）与 onoma（名字）构成。

items.en: Scholars of rhetoric use synonymum for words of related meaning.
items.cn: 修辞学者用拉丁语 synonymum 表示意义相关的词。

items.en: Forms close to Latin synonymum circulate in learned French writing.
items.cn: 接近拉丁语 synonymum 的词形在学术性法语写作中流传。

items.en: Synonym appears in English, often paired with antonym in word lists for pupils.
items.cn: synonym 进入英语，常与 antonym 一起出现在给学生的词汇表里。

items.en: Dictionaries add synonym sections, and biology adopts the word for duplicate scientific names.
items.cn: 词典增设同义词栏目，生物学也用这个词指重复的学名。

note.en: Synonym shares the Greek parts syn and onoma with antonym, homonym, and pseudonym, and sits near the everyday words for equivalent wording.
note.cn: synonym 与 antonym、homonym、pseudonym 共享希腊语成分 syn 与 onoma，意义上也与表示「等义说法」的日常词相邻。

entries.definition: a word with the opposite meaning
entries.definitionCN: 反义词；与 synonym 共享 -onym，以 anti 代替 syn

entries.definition: a word spelled or pronounced like another but different in meaning
entries.definitionCN: 同形或同音异义词；由 homos（相同）加 -onym 构成

entries.definition: having the same or a very close meaning
entries.definitionCN: 同义的；意义相同的

entries.definition: a word or thing equal in meaning or value to another
entries.definitionCN: 等值物；意义或价值相当的说法

entries.definition: a different form of the same word or thing
entries.definitionCN: 同一词或事物的另一种形式

entries.definition: a restatement of something in other words
entries.definitionCN: 用别的说法重述

normalIntro.en: Synonym keeps the Greek pieces syn, together, and onoma, name, so the word itself says two names for one thing.
normalIntro.cn: synonym 保留希腊语成分 syn（一起）与 onoma（名字），这个词本身就在说「两个名字同指一物」。

normal.en: Syn means together in Greek, as in synonym and synthesis.
normal.cn: 希腊语 syn 表示「一起」，synonym 与 synthesis 里都有它。

normal.en: Onoma means name, and it also hides in anonymous, a name-less work.
normal.cn: onoma 表示「名字」，anonymous（无名的）里也藏着它。

normal.en: Swap syn for anti with its short i and you get antonym, the opposite word.
normal.cn: 把 syn 换成带短 i 的 anti，就得到 antonym 这个反义词。

normal.en: The adjective synonymous means equal in meaning, as in two synonymous terms.
normal.cn: 形容词 synonymous 表示「同义的」，如 two synonymous terms（两个同义说法）。

normal.en: The phrase a synonym for quality shows the byword sense of the word.
normal.cn: 短语 a synonym for quality（优质的代名词）体现了这个词的「代名词」义项。

abstract.en: Picture two differently cut keys that still turn the same lock.
abstract.cn: 想象两把齿形不同的钥匙，却都能打开同一把锁。

abstract.en: Imagine a thesaurus page where one line holds a whole row of twin words.
abstract.cn: 想象词典里的一行，写满了一串彼此成对的词。

abstract.en: Think of a shop sign on which two brand names hang from the very same hook.
abstract.cn: 想象一块招牌，两个品牌名挂在同一个钩子上。

examples.en: Phrases like a synonym for success are common in advertising copy.
examples.cn: 像「成功的代名词」这样的说法在广告文案里很常见。

examples.en: A good file of synonyms helps you avoid repeating the same word.
examples.cn: 整理得好的同义词资料能帮你避免重复同一个词。

examples.en: The two adjectives are close but not exact synonyms.
examples.cn: 这两个形容词意思接近，但并不完全同义。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喜弄呢」——两个词名一起被「弄」到一块儿，意思相通；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 syn（一起）+ onoma（名字）→ synonymos（同名的）→ 拉丁语 synonymum → 英语 synonym，核心义「共用一个名字」；同族词有 antonym、homonym、pseudonym、anonymous。

sensesIntro.en: Synonym first names a word with the same meaning, widens to near words and bywords, and ends as a technical label in taxonomy.
sensesIntro.cn: synonym 先指意义相同的词，进而放宽为近义词与「代名词」，最后在分类学里成为专门的术语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two keys of different shape that open one lock.
core.cn: 核心意象：两把形状不同的钥匙开同一把锁。

branches.en: A word with the same meaning is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 意义相同的词是日常义项。

branches.en: Near words and bywords loosen the tie from exact sameness to habitual association.
branches.cn: 近义词与代名词把「完全等同」放宽为「意义相近或习惯关联」。

branches.en: A duplicate scientific name is the specialist sense of one label for one thing.
branches.cn: 重复的学名是专门义项，同样是一个对象配两个名称。

branches.en: Dictionaries list synonyms and near synonyms in the same column.
branches.cn: 词典把同义词与近义词列在同一栏里。

branches.en: Both a byword and a taxonomic synonym let one familiar label stand for something else.
branches.cn: 代名词与分类学同名都让一个熟悉的名称代替另一样东西。

intro.en: Synonym is built from the Greek combining elements syn and onym, which also shape antonym, homonym, and the suffix -onym.
intro.cn: synonym 由希腊语组合成分 syn 与 onym 构成，这两个成分也塑造了 antonym、homonym 与后缀 -onym。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word as synonymum, and scholarly French passed it to English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把希腊语词借作 synonymum，学术性法语再把它传给英语。

items.example: Syn links words that belong together.
items.exampleCN: syn 把意义上属于一起的词连起来。

items.example: Onoma supplies the name element.
items.exampleCN: onoma 提供「名字」这个成分。

items.example: The suffix -onym names word relationships.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -onym 用于表示词与词的关系。

items.example: Antonym swaps syn for anti.
items.exampleCN: antonym 把 syn 换成了 anti。

items.meaning: a word sounding or spelled like another
items.example: Homonym uses homos for same.
items.exampleCN: homonym 用 homos 表示「相同」。

items.example: Anonymous adds a- for without.
items.exampleCN: anonymous 加上表示「没有」的 a-。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms synonymous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 构成 synonymous。

items.example: Synonymous describes equal meaning.
items.exampleCN: synonymous 描述意义相同。

items.example: Synonymy names the relation of sameness.
items.exampleCN: synonymy 指「同义」这种关系。

latinEntries.meaning: a word of the same meaning

definition_zh: 句法；语法；句法结构；语法规则
definition_en: the way words are arranged and connected to form sentences in a language, and the rules governing that arrangement
core_image: 一排积木按固定顺序搭好，才卡得住、不会散架
scene: 语法课上，老师把打乱的词写在黑板上，让学生重新排成一句通顺的话。In grammar class, the teacher scrambled words on the board and asked pupils to fix the syntax of the sentence.
sceneCN: 这里 syntax 是「句法、词序结构」（第 1 个义项：词语组合成句子的方式）；句意：语法课上，老师把黑板上的词打乱，让学生把句子的句法结构理顺。

derivatives.zh: 由 syntax 换 -t- 加 -ic 构成，义为「句法的」
由 syntactic 加 -ly 构成，义为「在句法上」
由 syntactic 加 -ian 构成，义为「句法学家」

senses.title: The arrangement of words
senses.definition: the way words are put together and ordered to build sentences
senses.definitionCN: 词语被组合并排列成句子的方式
senses.example: The teacher explained the syntax of question forms.
senses.exampleCN: 老师讲解了疑问句的句法。
senses.why: Greek syn means together and taxis means arranging, so syntax is the arranging of words into order.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 syn 意为「一起」，taxis 意为「排列」，所以句法就是把词语排列在一起的方式。

senses.title: The rules themselves
senses.definition: the set of rules that govern how words combine in a language
senses.definitionCN: 规定一个语言中词语如何组合的整套规则
senses.example: Children pick up the syntax of their language without formal lessons.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们不用正式上课就能学会母语的语法规则。
senses.why: From the act of arranging comes the rule system that decides which arrangements are allowed.
senses.whyCN: 由「排列」这个动作，进一步引申为决定哪些排列才合格的规则体系。

senses.title: The set of rules for a notation
senses.definition: the rules that say how the elements of a programming language may be written
senses.definitionCN: 规定编程语言的各个成分应如何书写的规则
senses.example: A missing bracket is a common syntax error in code.
senses.exampleCN: 少一个括号是代码中常见的语法错误。
senses.why: Programming languages also arrange symbols by rule, so the grammar word moved from words to code.
senses.whyCN: 编程语言同样按规则排列符号，于是这个语法词从词语扩展到了代码。

senses.title: Ordered structure in scholarship
senses.definition: an orderly system or formal structure of parts within a field of study
senses.definitionCN: 某学科中各个部分有序组成的体系
senses.example: Histories once described the syntax of institutions as the order of a whole age.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的史学曾把制度的「体系」描述为整个时代的秩序。
senses.why: The original image of arranging things in order survives in this rarer use for structured systems.
