senses.whyCN: 「把事物排成秩序」的原始意象，在这个较少见的「有结构的体系」用法中保留了下来。

intro.en: Syntax comes from Greek syntaxis, a putting in order or a drawing up of troops, built from syn, together, and taxis, arrangement.
intro.cn: syntax 来自希腊语 syntaxis（排列、布阵），由 syn（一起）与 taxis（排列）构成。

items.en: Syntaxis means a putting in order, often of troops in a line.
items.cn: 希腊语 syntaxis 意为「排列」，常指军队列阵。

items.en: Grammarians of Alexandria transfer the word to the ordering of words.
items.cn: 亚历山大里亚的语法学家把该词转到词语的排列上。

items.en: Latin syntax is used by grammarians for the fitting together of words.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语里，语法学家用 syntax 表示词语的配合。

items.en: French syntaxe circulates in grammatical treatises and from there into English.
items.cn: 法语 syntaxe 在语法论著中流行，并由此进入英语。

items.en: Modern linguistics and computing give syntax a central and technical role.
items.cn: 现代语言学与计算机学使 syntax 获得核心而专业化的地位。

note.en: Syntax pairs with the Greek combining elements syn and tax, and in meaning it sits close to words about grammar and word order.
note.cn: syntax 与希腊语组合成分 syn、tax 相配，在意义上与表示「语法、词序」的词相邻。

entries.definition: relating to the arrangement of words
entries.definitionCN: 句法的；与词序结构有关的

entries.definition: the plural of the word for word order systems
entries.definitionCN: 表示多种句法体系的复数形式

entries.definition: the ordered classification of living things
entries.definitionCN: 生物的次序分类；与 syntax 共享 taxis（排列）一词根

entries.definition: the rules for combining words into sentences
entries.definitionCN: 把词组合成句子的规则；范围比 syntax 更宽

entries.definition: the sequence in which words are placed
entries.definitionCN: 词在句子中排列的次序

entries.definition: the study of the internal forms of words
entries.definitionCN: 词形学；研究词内部结构，与句法互补

normalIntro.en: Syntax keeps the Greek pieces syn, together, and taxis, arrangement, so the word reads as the arranging of words together.
normalIntro.cn: syntax 保留希腊语成分 syn（一起）与 taxis（排列），整个词就是「把词一起排成序」。

normal.en: Syn in Greek means together, as it does in synonym and synthesis.
normal.cn: 希腊语 syn 意为「一起」，在 synonym 和 synthesis 里也是这个意思。

normal.en: Taxis means arrangement, and the same element survives in taxonomy.
normal.cn: taxis 意为「排列」，同一个成分也保留在 taxonomy（分类学）里。

normal.en: Change the x to ct for the adjective syntactic, as in syntactic analysis.
normal.cn: 把 x 换成 ct 就得到形容词 syntactic，如 syntactic analysis（句法分析）。

normal.en: A syntax error in code means the order of symbols is not allowed.
normal.cn: 代码里的 syntax error（语法错误）就是符号的顺序不被允许。

normal.en: Grammar is the wider field, and syntax is its sentence-building part.
normal.cn: grammar（语法）范围更广，syntax 是其中负责造句的那部分。

abstract.en: Picture blocks that only lock together when they sit in the right order.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆积木，只有按正确顺序摆好才卡得住。

abstract.en: Imagine a train whose carriages must be joined in a fixed sequence.
abstract.cn: 想象一列火车，车厢必须按固定顺序连接。

abstract.en: Think of dancers who keep perfect rows while they move across the stage.
abstract.cn: 想象舞者在台上来回走位，却始终保持着整齐的队形。

examples.en: English syntax usually places the verb after the subject.
examples.cn: 英语句法通常把动词放在主语之后。

examples.en: The translator compared the syntax of the two languages.
examples.cn: 译者比较了这两种语言的句法。

examples.en: Fix the syntax before you worry about style.
examples.cn: 先把句法理清，再去操心文风。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「新塔克斯」——把一块块新积木按「克斯」的次序排好，就成了一句有秩序的话；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 syn（一起）+ taxis（排列）→ syntaxis（排列；布阵）→ 晚期拉丁语 syntax → 法语 syntaxe → 英语 syntax，核心义「把词语排成序」；同族词有 syntactic、taxonomy。

sensesIntro.en: Syntax begins with the arrangement of words, becomes the rule system behind it, and grows into the grammar of code and the ordered structure of a field.
sensesIntro.cn: syntax 先指词语的排列方式，进而指背后的规则体系，再扩展到代码的语法与学科的秩序结构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: blocks that lock into place only in the right order.
core.cn: 核心意象：积木只有按正确次序摆好才能卡住。

branches.en: The ordering of words is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 词语的排列方式是日常义项。

branches.en: The rule set that governs the ordering is the grammar sense.
branches.cn: 支配排列的规则体系是语法层面的义项。

branches.en: Programming languages reuse the word for symbol rules.
branches.cn: 编程语言把该词用于符号规则，形成计算机义项。

branches.en: Ordered structure in a discipline keeps the old image of arranged parts.
branches.cn: 学科中的秩序结构保留了「部件有序排列」的旧意象。

branches.en: Both a sentence and a line of code fail when the pieces sit in the wrong place.
branches.cn: 句子与代码行都会因部件位置不对而失败。

intro.en: Syntax is a Greek compound of syn and tax, with English adjectives and nouns built on the stem syntact-.
intro.cn: syntax 是 syn 与 tax 构成的希腊语复合词，英语在 syntact- 这一词干上造出形容词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin grammarians took over the Greek word as syntax, from which French and English inherited it.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语语法学家沿用希腊语词形作 syntax，法语与英语由此继承。

items.example: Syn marks things placed together.
items.exampleCN: syn 标示被放在一起的东西。

items.example: Taxis supplies the ordering idea.
items.exampleCN: taxis 提供「排列」的概念。

items.example: The suffix -tactic forms the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -tactic 构成形容词。

items.example: Syntactic describes sentence structure.
items.exampleCN: syntactic 描述句子结构。

items.example: The suffix -ally forms syntactically.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ally 构成 syntactically。

items.example: Syntactically describes sentence structure.
items.exampleCN: syntactically 描述句子在句法层面的特征。

items.example: The suffix -ian forms syntactician.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ian 构成 syntactician。

items.example: Syntactician names a grammar specialist.
items.exampleCN: syntactician 指研究句法的专家。

items.example: Taxonomy shares the ordering root.
items.exampleCN: taxonomy 共享「排列」这一词根。

latinEntries.meaning: arrangement, a drawing up in order

definition_zh: 糖浆；糖水；果酱浆；（加糖浆调制的）饮品；糖浆状液体
definition_en: a thick, sweet liquid made by dissolving sugar in water or boiled down from fruit juice, often eaten with pancakes or added to drinks
core_image: 一勺浓糖浆缓缓倾下，在盘沿拉出细亮的长丝
scene: 早餐的餐桌上，孩子把糖浆淋在松饼上，盘子边很快积了一小汪。At the breakfast table, the child poured syrup over the pancakes and a small pool gathered at the rim of the plate.
sceneCN: 这里 syrup 是「糖浆」（第 1 个义项：由糖与水熬成的浓稠甜液）；句意：早餐桌上，孩子把糖浆淋在松饼上，盘子边缘很快积起了一小汪。

derivatives.zh: 由 syrup 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「糖浆似的；黏稠甜腻的」
由 syrupy 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「黏稠甜腻的状态」
与 syrup 同源于阿拉伯语「饮料」一词，义为「（水果）雪泥、冰糕」

senses.title: Thick sweet liquid
senses.definition: a thick sweet liquid made from sugar and water or from fruit juice
senses.definitionCN: 用糖水或果汁熬成的浓稠甜液
senses.example: She poured maple syrup over the warm pancakes.
senses.exampleCN: 她往热松饼上淋了枫糖浆。
senses.why: The Arabic source meant a drink, and boiled sugar water keeps that drinking image in a thick form.
senses.whyCN: 阿拉伯语词源意为「饮料」，熬煮的糖水保留了这个「喝的」意象，只是变得浓稠。

senses.title: Sweet fruit preserve
senses.definition: fruit cooked with sugar until thick, eaten with bread or dessert
senses.definitionCN: 加糖煮浓的水果制品，配面包或甜点食用
senses.example: The label on the jar read orchard berry syrup.
senses.exampleCN: 罐子上的标签写着「果园浆果酱」。
senses.why: Fruit boiled down thickens into a syrup, so the word covers jam-like preserves as well.
senses.whyCN: 水果熬煮加浓后变成糖浆状，所以这个词也涵盖果酱一类的制品。

senses.title: Sweet drink base
senses.definition: a sweetened drink or the flavoured liquid mixed with water or soda to make one
senses.definitionCN: 甜味的饮品，或兑水、兑苏打水做成饮品的调味糖液
senses.example: The shop sells bottles of strawberry syrup for soda water.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店卖一瓶瓶草莓糖浆，用来兑苏打水做饮品。
senses.why: The old sense of a sweet drink survives in flavoured syrups that people dilute into a glass.
senses.whyCN: 「甜饮料」的旧义残留在调味糖浆里，人们把它兑开成一杯饮品。

senses.title: Gooey or over-sweet
senses.titleCN: 甜腻的；过分甜软的东西
senses.definition: something cloyingly sweet, sticky, or sentimental in style
senses.definitionCN: 甜得发腻、黏腻或风格过分煽情的东西
senses.example: The film drips with syrup in its final love scene.
senses.exampleCN: 这部片子的最后一场爱情戏甜得发腻。
senses.why: A liquid this sweet and sticky naturally supplies the image of anything cloying, including style.
senses.whyCN: 如此甜腻黏稠的液体，自然成了「腻人」意象的由来，连文风也能这样形容。

intro.en: Syrup goes back through Old French sirop to Arabic charab, a sweet drink, ultimately from the verb shariba, to drink.
intro.cn: syrup 经古法语 sirop 追溯到阿拉伯语 charab（甜饮料），最终源自动词 shariba（喝）。

items.en: Charab names a sweet drink, from shariba, to drink.
items.cn: 印度阿拉伯语 charab 指甜饮料，源于 shariba（喝）。

items.en: Physicians write syrupus for the thick sugar-water medicines of the period.
items.cn: 中世纪医生用拉丁语 syrupus 指当时浓稠的糖水药剂。

items.en: Sirop enters Old French from the Italian or Latin form of the word.
items.cn: sirop 经意大利语或拉丁语形式进入古法语。

items.en: Syrup appears in English, at first for sweet medicines and drinks.
items.cn: syrup 进入英语，最初指甜味药水与甜饮。

items.en: Syrup spreads to maple toppings, fruit preserves, and soda bases.
items.cn: 现代英语里 syrup 扩展到枫糖浇汁、果酱制品与汽水糖液。

note.en: Syrup comes from the Arabic root for drinking and sits close to sweet liquid words such as molasses and marmalade.
note.cn: syrup 源自阿拉伯语「喝」的词根，意义上与 molasses、marmalade 等甜味液体词相邻。

entries.definition: thick and sweet like syrup
entries.definitionCN: 糖浆般黏稠甜腻的

entries.definition: a frozen sweet or a fruit drink
entries.definitionCN: （水果）雪泥冰糕；与 syrup 同出阿拉伯语「饮料」一词

entries.definition: a frozen dessert of fruit juice
entries.definitionCN: 雪葩、果汁冰糕；与 syrup 同源，只是拼写走的另一条路

entries.definition: thick dark syrup left after sugar refining
entries.definitionCN: 糖蜜；制糖后的浓稠深色糖浆

entries.definition: a thick dark syrup in British use
entries.definitionCN: 英式用法里的深色糖浆

entries.definition: a preserve of citrus fruit with sugar
entries.definitionCN: 柑橘果酱；同类甜味制品

normalIntro.en: Syrup carries the Arabic word for a sweet drink that trickled into European kitchens through medicine.
normalIntro.cn: syrup 带着阿拉伯语「甜饮料」一词，一路经医学配方流进了欧洲的厨房。

normal.en: Maple syrup names the classic topping poured on pancakes.
normal.cn: maple syrup（枫糖浆）就是往松饼上淋的经典浇汁。

normal.en: Corn syrup is the sweetener hidden in many drinks.
normal.cn: corn syrup（玉米糖浆）是许多饮料里隐藏的甜味剂。

normal.en: Cough syrup keeps the old medical use of sweet thick liquid.
normal.cn: cough syrup（止咳糖浆）保留了这个词古老的药用含义。

normal.en: Add -y for syrupy, meaning sticky and over-sweet.
normal.cn: 加上 -y 得到 syrupy，表示「黏稠又甜腻」。

normal.en: Compare molasses: it is a syrup by-product, but a darker one.
normal.cn: 对比 molasses（糖蜜）：它也是一种糖浆副产品，只是颜色更深。

abstract.en: Picture a spoon lifting a slow golden ribbon that never breaks.
abstract.cn: 想象一勺糖浆提起一条缓缓垂落、始终不断的金色细带。

abstract.en: Imagine a pancake stack turning glossy as the syrup spreads.
abstract.cn: 想象糖浆铺开时，一摞松饼渐渐泛起油亮的光。

abstract.en: Think of a spoon left in the jar and slowly sinking.
abstract.cn: 想象一把勺子插在罐里，正缓缓往下沉。

examples.en: The puddings are served with warm orange syrup.
examples.cn: 这些布丁配温热的橙子糖浆上桌。

examples.en: Stir the sugar until it becomes a thick syrup.
examples.cn: 把糖搅到它变成浓稠的糖浆为止。

examples.en: He gave the child a spoonful of honey syrup for his sore throat.
examples.cn: 他给孩子喂了一勺蜂蜜糖浆，缓解喉咙痛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吸着泼」——浓糖浆怎么吸、怎么顺都黏着盘沿「泼」不下去；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 印度阿拉伯语 charab（甜饮料，源自 shariba「喝」）→ 中世纪拉丁语 syrupus（糖水药剂）→ 古法语 sirop → 英语 syrup，核心义「熬浓的甜液」。

sensesIntro.en: Syrup starts as a thick sugar liquid, extends to fruit preserves and drink bases, and finally figures anything cloyingly sweet.
sensesIntro.cn: syrup 先指浓稠的糖液，扩展到果酱制品与饮品糖基，最后引申指任何「甜得发腻」的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spoon of thick golden liquid trailing a bright thread.
core.cn: 核心意象：一勺金色浓液拉出细细的亮丝。

branches.en: Thick sugar liquid is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 浓稠的糖液是日常义项。

branches.en: Fruit preserves and drink bases extend the liquid to foods and drinks.
branches.cn: 果酱制品与饮品糖基把这种液体扩展到食物与饮料。

branches.en: The cloying sense turns the physical stickiness into a quality.
branches.cn: 「腻」的义项把物理上的黏稠转化成了品质。

branches.en: Both a sugar syrup and a fruit preserve are boiled down and kept thick.
branches.cn: 糖浆与果酱制品都要熬浓、保持黏稠。

branches.en: A soda base and a fussy film scene both invite the image of too much sweetness.
branches.cn: 调制汽水的糖液与过火的电影场景都唤起「甜过头」的意象。

intro.en: Syrup is a borrowing with no productive prefix or suffix in English, though -y and -ness build syrupy and syrupiness from it.
intro.cn: syrup 是借词，英语里没有可再复用的前缀或后缀，但能借 -y、-ness 构成 syrupy、syrupiness。

latinIntro.en: The word reached Europe as Medieval Latin syrupus, but its deepest root is the Arabic verb for drinking.
latinIntro.cn: 该词以中世纪拉丁语 syrupus 的形式传入欧洲，但更深的词根是阿拉伯语中「喝」的动词。

items.example: Syrup keeps its borrowed shape whole.
items.exampleCN: syrup 完整保留借来的词形。

items.example: The suffix -y forms syrupy from the noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 在名词基础上构成 syrupy。

items.example: Syrupy describes a thick, sweet texture.
items.exampleCN: syrupy 描述黏稠甜腻的质感。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms syrupiness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 syrupiness。

items.example: Syrupiness names an over-sweet quality.
items.exampleCN: syrupiness 指过分甜腻的性质。

items.example: Shariba is the deepest source of the word.
items.exampleCN: shariba 是该词最深的来源。

items.example: Charab is a sweet drink, not a solid sweet.
items.exampleCN: charab 指甜饮料，而不是固体甜食。

items.example: Syrupus was a physician word for sugar medicine.
items.exampleCN: syrupus 是医生对糖水药剂的称呼。

latinEntries.meaning: a sweet syrup or sugar medicine
a variant spelling of the same medicine word
latinEntries.meaningCN: 同一药剂词的另一拼写形式

definition_zh: 禁忌；忌讳；避讳；列为禁忌
definition_en: something that a culture forbids people to say or do
core_image: 部落祭坛上插着一块木牌，木牌写着不许碰
scene: 族里的老人说，祖先留下的地方不可随意踏入。The elders warned that the sacred ground was taboo and must never be entered.
sceneCN: 这里 taboo 是「禁忌」（第 1 个义项：文化中被禁止触碰或谈论的事物）；句意：族里的老人警告说，那片圣地是禁忌，绝不能踏入。

derivatives.zh: 被列为禁忌的，源自动词 taboo 的过去分词加 -ed
忌禁风俗，由 taboo 加名词后缀 -ism 构成
未经禁忌的，由前缀 un- 加 tabooed 构成

senses.title: A socially forbidden subject or act
senses.definition: something a culture or group forbids people to discuss, touch, or do
senses.definitionCN: 某一文化或群体禁止人们谈论、触碰或去做的事物
senses.example: In many cultures, asking about a person income is a taboo.
senses.exampleCN: 在不少文化里，打听别人的收入是一种禁忌。
senses.why: The Tongan word tabu meant set apart for the gods, and what is set apart must not be touched.
senses.whyCN: 汤加语 tabu 原指「为神而单独隔开」，凡被隔开的东西便不可触碰，于是长成了「禁忌」。

senses.title: The adjective marking a forbidden thing
senses.definition: used to describe a subject, word, or act that a group marks as forbidden
senses.definitionCN: 用来描述被某群体标记为禁止的话题、词语或行为
senses.example: Death remains a taboo topic at the dinner table.
senses.exampleCN: 在餐桌上，死亡仍是一个禁忌话题。
senses.why: Once people keep a thing apart, the word turns into a label that we place in front of the thing.
senses.whyCN: 一旦人们把某事物隔开，这个词就转为贴在事物前面的标签，充当形容词。

senses.title: To mark something as forbidden
senses.definition: to declare that something must not be spoken of or done
senses.definitionCN: 宣布某事不可谈论或不可去做
senses.example: The village tabooed hunting in the forest for a whole year.
senses.exampleCN: 村子把森林里的狩猎列为禁忌，整整一年不许进行。
senses.why: If a custom can set something apart, a council can also do it on purpose, so the noun grew a verb use.
senses.whyCN: 既然习俗能把某物隔开，议事会也能刻意这么做，于是名词又生出了动词用法。

senses.title: The word that may not be spoken
senses.definition: a word that a group avoids saying aloud, often out of respect or fear
senses.definitionCN: 某群体因敬畏或害怕而避免说出口的词语
senses.example: Some languages use a taboo for the name of a dead king.
senses.exampleCN: 有些语言会把已故君主的名字当作忌讳词来回避。
senses.why: Being set apart applies to names too, so certain words become unusable and a substitute is chosen instead.
senses.whyCN: 「被隔开」也适用于名字，某些词因此不能使用，人们改用别的说法代替。

intro.en: Taboo entered English from the Pacific: it comes from Tongan tapu, and the English form reflects Captain Cook writing what he heard.
intro.cn: taboo 从太平洋进入英语：它源自汤加语 tapu，英语拼写反映了库克船长听写时的记音。

items.en: Tapu means set apart or under a sacred restriction.
items.cn: tapu 意为被隔开、受神圣限制。

items.en: Captain Cook recorded the word during his voyages in the Pacific.
items.cn: 库克船长在太平洋航行中记录下这个词。

items.en: English spelled it taboo and used it for sacred prohibitions.
items.cn: 英语将其写作 taboo，用来指神圣的禁令。

items.en: Missionaries and travellers spread it into other Pacific languages.
items.cn: 传教士与旅行者把它带到其他太平洋语言中。

items.en: It spread from religious restriction to any social ban.
items.cn: 它从宗教性的禁令扩展到一切社会禁令。

note.en: Taboo looks close to other Pacific words and sits beside ordinary prohibition words.
note.cn: taboo 与若干太平洋语言词形相近，并与平常表示「禁止」的词相邻。

entries.definition: the Tongan word for sacred and set apart
entries.definitionCN: 汤加语中表示神圣、隔开的原词

entries.definition: the past participle, meaning marked as forbidden
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，意为被列为禁忌的；由本词加 -ed 构成

entries.definition: an older variant spelling of taboo
entries.definitionCN: taboo 的旧式异体拼写；与本词同源

entries.definition: to strike lightly; only the two letters are alike, the origin is different
entries.definitionCN: 轻敲；只是拼写巧合，词源不同

entries.definition: an official order forbidding something
entries.definitionCN: 禁令；正式禁止

entries.definition: a law or rule that forbids something
entries.definitionCN: 禁止；禁令

entries.definition: a belief in luck or magic rather than reason
entries.definitionCN: 迷信

normalIntro.en: Taboo is a Pacific word for anything set apart, so the memory hook is the barrier around the sacred.
normalIntro.cn: taboo 是表示「被隔开」的太平洋词，记忆抓手就是围着神圣之物的那道界线。

normal.en: A taboo subject is one that a group refuses to discuss.
normal.cn: a taboo subject 指一个群体拒绝讨论的话题。

normal.en: To break a taboo is to do what the group forbids.
normal.cn: break a taboo 就是做了该群体禁止的事。

normal.en: The word came from Tonga, brought back by Captain Cook.
normal.cn: 这个词来自汤加，由库克船长带回。

normal.en: The plural taboos and the past form tabooed both keep the silent ending.
normal.cn: 复数 taboos 与过去式 tabooed 都保留了这个词的拼写。

normal.en: Death, money, and politics are common taboo topics in polite talk.
normal.cn: 死亡、金钱与政治是客套谈话里常见的禁忌话题。

abstract.en: Picture a rope across a path with a wooden sign hanging from it.
abstract.cn: 想象小路上横着一根绳，绳上挂着一块木牌。

abstract.en: Picture a word written on a slate, then wiped away before it is spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词写在石板上，在说出口之前就被擦掉。

abstract.en: Hear a council member standing up and saying that a custom is now closed.
abstract.cn: 想象议事会成员起身宣布：某项习俗从此封闭。

examples.en: Religion is often a taboo subject in casual conversation.
examples.cn: 在日常闲聊中，宗教常常是禁忌话题。

examples.en: The community tabooed the names of the dead.
examples.cn: 这个社群把死者的名字列为禁忌。

examples.en: Some societies treat the left hand as taboo.
examples.cn: 有些社会把左手视为禁忌。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「套布」——把神圣的祭坛套上一层布，隔着布谁也不许碰；这只是谐音联想，与汤加语的词源无关。

root: 汤加语 tapu（被隔开、神圣受限）→ 库克船长记作 taboo → 英语 taboo（禁忌）→ 引申为「禁忌的」「把……列为禁忌」。

sensesIntro.en: Taboo begins as a noun for a forbidden thing, becomes an adjective marking such things, grows a verb of declaring a ban, and finally covers the unspeakable word itself.
sensesIntro.cn: taboo 先作名词指被禁止的事物，再作形容词标记这类事物，又长出表示「宣布禁令」的动词，最后也指不能出口的那个词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sign hanging on a rope that keeps people away.
core.cn: 核心意象：绳上挂着的木牌，把人挡在外面。

branches.en: A forbidden subject is the plain noun sense.
branches.cn: 被禁止的话题是名词的平常用法。

branches.en: Marking a topic as forbidden gives the adjective use.
branches.cn: 把话题标记为禁止，就得到形容词用法。

branches.en: Declaring the ban gives the verb use.
branches.cn: 宣布禁令，就有了动词用法。

branches.en: The noun covers both a forbidden act and the word that must not be said.
branches.cn: 名词既指被禁止的行为，也指不能说的词。

branches.en: Adjective and verb both point at the moment of setting something apart.
branches.cn: 形容词与动词都指向「把某物隔开」的那一刻。

intro.en: Taboo is a borrowed Pacific word rather than a Latin root, so its family is small and English-built.
intro.cn: taboo 是借自太平洋语言的词，而非拉丁词根，因此词族很小，且多为英语自造。

latinIntro.en: No Latin origin is known for taboo; its source is Tongan tapu.
latinIntro.cn: taboo 并无已知的拉丁语来源，它的源头是汤加语 tapu。

items.example: Tabu is the source of the English form.
items.exampleCN: tabu 是英语形式的来源。

items.meaning: the sound of the borrowed word
items.example: The ending -oo records the long vowel heard at sea.
items.exampleCN: 结尾 -oo 记录的是海上听来的长元音。

items.example: Taboo names what a group avoids.
items.exampleCN: taboo 指一个群体回避的事物。

items.example: A taboo word is one people will not say.
items.exampleCN: taboo word 指人们不肯说的词。

items.example: The suffix -ed builds the participle tabooed.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成过去分词 tabooed。

items.example: The suffix -ing builds tabooing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 tabooing。

items.example: The plural taboos adds -s to the noun.
items.exampleCN: 复数 taboos 由名词加 -s 得到。

items.example: The suffix -ism forms tabooism.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 构成 tabooism。

definition_zh: 心照不宣的；默示的；不言而喻的
definition_en: expressed without being said aloud, because it is understood by everyone
core_image: 两人并肩做事，谁也不开口，却都懂
scene: 他们从没签过合同，只是年复一年互相帮忙。They never signed a contract; their help rested on a tacit agreement.
sceneCN: 这里 tacit 是「心照不宣的」（第 1 个义项：无需明说而被理解的）；句意：他们从未签过合同，彼此的帮助建立在一份心照不宣的约定之上。

pos.zh: 心照不宣的；默示的；不言而喻的

derivatives.zh: 默默地；心照不宣地，由 tacit 加副词后缀 -ly 构成
默许性；不言之性，由 tacit 加名词后缀 -ness 构成
沉默寡言的；与 tacit 同词源，源自动词 taceo
缄默的；由前缀 re- 加同源词干构成

senses.title: Understood without being spoken
senses.definition: understood or meant by everyone involved, though never put into words
senses.definitionCN: 所有相关的人都明白，却从未说出口
senses.example: Years of sharing a kitchen created a tacit understanding between them.
senses.exampleCN: 多年共用一个厨房，让他们之间形成了默契。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to be silent, so the core image is understanding that needs no voice.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「沉默」，因此核心意象是无需出声也懂的理解。

senses.title: Approval given by silence
senses.definition: approval that is shown by saying nothing rather than by saying yes
senses.definitionCN: 用沉默而不是用肯定的答复来表示的同意
senses.example: Her absence at the meeting was read as tacit approval.
senses.exampleCN: 她在会上的缺席被理解为默许。
senses.why: Silence is not always a refusal; it can do the work of a yes, which is exactly what tacit names.
senses.whyCN: 沉默并不总是拒绝，它也能起到「同意」的作用，而 tacit 命名的正是这种沉默。

senses.title: Knowledge that is not written down
senses.definition: describing knowledge that is picked up by doing rather than by reading
senses.definitionCN: 形容通过实践而非阅读习得的知识
senses.example: A chef carries a great deal of tacit knowledge in the hands, not in notes.
senses.exampleCN: 厨师把大量隐性知识放在手上，而不是写在笔记里。
senses.why: What is never spoken is also never written down, so the word moved into the study of learning.
senses.whyCN: 从未说出口的东西也不会写下来，于是这个词进入了对学习的研究。

intro.en: Tacit comes from Latin tacere, to be silent, through the adjective tacitus, meaning not spoken of.
intro.cn: tacit 来自拉丁语 tacere（沉默），经由形容词 tacitus（未说出口的）。

items.en: Tacere means to be silent or to keep quiet.
items.cn: tacere 意为沉默、不作声。

items.en: Tacitus is the habit of keeping silent, built from the same verb.
items.cn: tacitus 是保持沉默的习惯，由同一动词构成。

items.en: The adjective tacit means passed over in silence, unmentioned.
items.cn: 形容词 tacit 意为被沉默地带过、未提及。

items.en: English takes tacit from Latin for agreements left unsaid.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语从拉丁语引入 tacit，专指未说出口的约定。

items.en: It widens to approval by silence and knowledge held in the body.
items.cn: 它扩展到默许，以及储存在身心之中的知识。

note.en: Tacit belongs to the Latin family of silence, tacere and tacitus, and sits beside words that say what is not said.
note.cn: tacit 属于拉丁语中表示沉默的词族 tacere、tacitus，并与「言而不尽」的相关词相邻。

entries.definition: in a way that is understood but not spoken
entries.definitionCN: 默默地；心照不宣地

entries.definition: silent by nature; built from the Latin verb taceo
entries.definitionCN: 天生沉默寡言的；由拉丁语动词 taceo 构成

entries.definition: slow to speak; the stem comes from Latin tacere
entries.definitionCN: 说话有保留的；词干源自拉丁语 tacere

entries.definition: skill in saying the right thing; it comes from tangere, to touch, so only the spelling is alike
entries.definitionCN: 说话得体；词源为 tangere（触摸），只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: suggested rather than stated directly
entries.definitionCN: 含蓄的；暗含的

entries.definition: not said aloud though felt
entries.definitionCN: 没说出口的

entries.definition: meant without being put into words
entries.definitionCN: 隐含的；不言明的

normalIntro.en: Tacit keeps the Latin picture of silence, so remember it as understanding with the sound turned off.
normalIntro.cn: tacit 保留了拉丁语中沉默的画面，可以把它记成「关掉声音也懂」的理解。

normal.en: A tacit agreement is one that nobody writes down.
normal.cn: tacit agreement 指谁也没有写下来的约定。

normal.en: Tacit approval comes from silence, not from a speech.
normal.cn: tacit approval 来自沉默，而不来自表态。

normal.en: Tacit knowledge lives in practice, such as riding a bike.
normal.cn: tacit knowledge 存在于实践中，比如骑车。

normal.en: The adverb tacitly adds -ly to say that it is done silently.
normal.cn: 副词 tacitly 加副词后缀表示默默地做。

normal.en: Compare implicit: implicit can mark a hidden logic, while tacit marks agreement and knowledge
normal.cn: 对比 implicit：implicit 可指隐藏的逻辑，tacit 多指约定与知识。

abstract.en: Picture two people building a wall side by side and never speaking.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人并排砌墙，从头到尾一句不说。

abstract.en: Picture a nod over the dinner table instead of a speech.
abstract.cn: 想象饭桌对面只是点了点头，而不是一番讲话。

abstract.en: Picture a cook whose hands know the dough better than any recipe.
abstract.cn: 想象一位厨师，双手比任何食谱更懂面团。

examples.en: They reached a tacit agreement about sharing the costs.
examples.cn: 他们就分摊费用达成了一种默契。

examples.en: Her long silence was taken as tacit consent.
examples.cn: 她长时间的沉默被视为默许。

examples.en: Good teachers pass on a great deal of tacit knowledge.
examples.cn: 好老师会传递大量隐性知识。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「它静」——他一开口就安静，什么都不必说，大家却都懂了；这只是谐音联想，与拉丁语词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tacere（沉默）→ tacitus（沉默的；不提的）→ 拉丁语 tacit（被略过不提的）→ 英语 tacit（心照不宣的；默许的）。

sensesIntro.en: Tacit begins with what is understood but never said, then covers approval given by silence, and finally knowledge that is not written down.
sensesIntro.cn: tacit 先指无需说出口的领会，再指以沉默表示的同意，最后指未写下来的知识。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people working side by side with no need to speak.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人并肩做事，无需开口。

branches.en: Understanding without speech is the central sense.
branches.cn: 无言的领会是中心义项。

branches.en: A yes given by silence is the approval sense.
branches.cn: 以沉默表示的同意是默许义项。

branches.en: Knowledge held in the hands is the extended sense.
branches.cn: 存在双手中的知识是延伸义项。

branches.en: Both rest on a silence that everyone reads the same way.
branches.cn: 两者都依赖所有人都读得懂的沉默。

branches.en: An agreement without words and a skill without notes share the same silence.
branches.cn: 无言的约定与无笔记的技能共享同一种沉默。

intro.en: Tacit has a small Latin family around silence, with English adverbs and nouns built on top.
intro.cn: tacit 的拉丁词族围绕着「沉默」，英语又在它之上构成副词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin tacere means to be silent, and its family supplies tacit, taciturn, and reticent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tacere 意为沉默，其词族提供了 tacit、taciturn 与 reticent。

items.example: Tacere supplies the picture of quiet.
items.exampleCN: tacere 提供「安静」的画面。

items.example: Tacitus is the Latin adjective of silence.
items.exampleCN: tacitus 是表示沉默的拉丁形容词。

items.example: Tacit keeps the silent partner picture.
items.exampleCN: tacit 保留「沉默的伙伴」画面。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms tacitly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 tacitly。

items.example: Tacitly describes doing something quietly.
items.exampleCN: tacitly 描述暗中做某事。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms tacitness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 tacitness。

items.example: Taciturn names a person who rarely speaks.
items.exampleCN: taciturn 指很少说话的人。

items.example: The prefix re- appears in reticent.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 出现在 reticent 中。

definition_zh: 策略；手段；战术
definition_en: a planned way of doing something in order to reach a goal
core_image: 棋手在棋盘上挪动一枚棋子，为后面的几步铺路
scene: 球队落后一球，教练在场边临时换上一名速度快的球员。With a minute left, the coach tried a bold tactic and sent on a fast winger.
sceneCN: 这里 tactic 是「策略」（第 1 个义项：为达成目标而采取的具体做法）；句意：只剩一分钟，教练用了一招大胆的策略，换上一位速度快的边锋。

derivatives.zh: 战术；策略；复数形式还能指作为学科研究的战术学
战术上的；由 tactic 加形容词后缀 -al 构成
战术家；由 tactic 加指人的后缀 -ian 构成
在战术上；由 tactical 加副词后缀 -ly 构成

senses.title: A planned move toward a goal
senses.definition: a particular action or plan chosen to achieve a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为实现某一目的而选择的特定行动或计划
senses.example: Postponing the vote was a clever tactic.
senses.exampleCN: 推迟表决是一个巧妙的策略。
senses.why: Greek taktike meant the art of arranging troops, so a tactic is one planned move in a larger plan.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 taktike 意为排兵布阵之术，故 tactic 是整体计划中的一个精心安排的动作。

senses.title: The art of handling armed forces
senses.definition: the method of moving soldiers, ships, or aircraft in battle
senses.definitionCN: 在战斗中调动士兵、舰船或飞机的具体方法
senses.example: Rapid flanking tactics won the battle in a single afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 快速的侧翼战术在一个下午内就赢下了这场战斗。
senses.why: The word began in the army, so its oldest sense still names the handling of forces on the ground.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起于军队，所以最古老的义项仍指在地面上调遣部队的方法。

senses.title: Ways that avoid the real issue
senses.definition: a way of acting, often only to gain time or to dodge a question
senses.definitionCN: 一种做法，常只为拖延时间或回避某个问题
senses.example: Changing the subject was only a delaying tactic.
senses.exampleCN: 转移话题只是一种拖延手法。
senses.why: If a tactic is just a planned move, it can also be a move that simply stalls instead of solving anything.
senses.whyCN: 既然策略只是一个计划好的动作，它也可以是单纯拖延、并不解决问题的动作。

intro.en: Tactic comes from Greek taktike, the art of arrangement, and reached English through Latin and French.
intro.cn: tactic 来自希腊语 taktike（排列之术），经拉丁语与法语进入英语。

items.en: Tassein means to arrange or to place in order.
items.cn: tassein 意为排列、按顺序放置。

items.en: Taktike is the art of arranging, especially troops.
items.cn: taktike 指排列之术，尤指排兵布阵。

items.en: Tactica enters Latin as the science of ordering soldiers.
items.cn: tactica 以部队调度之术的含义进入拉丁语。

items.en: Books on military order spread the Latin form.
items.cn: 讲述军事阵法的著作使这一拉丁形式流传开来。

items.en: English tactic means one arrangement or plan in action.
items.cn: 英语 tactic 指行动中的一种安排或计划。

note.en: Tactic shares the Greek root of arranging with tactics and tactical, and stands beside words for plan and method.
note.cn: tactic 与 tactics、tactical 共享希腊语「排列」词根，并与表示计划、方法的词相邻。

entries.definition: the plural of tactic, also the study of arranging forces
entries.definitionCN: tactic 的复数，也指研究部队调遣的学科

entries.definition: relating to planned moves
entries.definitionCN: 与策略安排有关的

entries.definition: someone skilled in planning moves
entries.definitionCN: 擅长谋划的人；由本词族加后缀构成

entries.definition: careful skill in saying the right thing; it comes from tangere, so only the spelling is alike
entries.definitionCN: 说话细心得体；词源为 tangere（触摸），只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the overall plan behind many moves
entries.definitionCN: 战略；总体计划

entries.definition: an orderly way of doing something
entries.definitionCN: 方法；做法

entries.definition: a clever trick used for advantage
entries.definitionCN: 花招；手腕

normalIntro.en: Tactic is one arranged move, so remember it as a piece placed on a board for the next step.
normalIntro.cn: tactic 是一次安排好的动作，可以把它记成棋盘上为下一步铺路的一枚棋子。

normal.en: A clever tactic is a planned move, not an accident.
normal.cn: a clever tactic 是计划好的动作，不是偶然。

normal.en: Delaying tactics push a decision further back.
normal.cn: delaying tactics 把决定往后推。

normal.en: Military tactics concern how forces move in battle.
normal.cn: military tactics 关注部队在战斗中如何运动。

normal.en: Changing tactics means trying a different plan.
normal.cn: change tactics 意为换一套办法。

normal.en: Strategy is the whole plan and tactic is one move inside it.
normal.cn: strategy 是整体计划，tactic 是其中的一步。

abstract.en: Picture a knight lifted off the board and set down somewhere new.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚骑士棋被拿起，放在棋盘上的新位置。

abstract.en: Picture a football coach whispering one word before the corner kick.
abstract.cn: 想象足球教练在角球前低声说了句话。

abstract.en: Picture a visitor asking a hard question and the host turning to the weather.
abstract.cn: 想象客人问了个难题，主人转头谈起了天气。

examples.en: Delay is a common tactic in contract talks.
examples.cn: 拖延在合同谈判中是常见策略。

examples.en: The general studied the hill tactics of his enemy.
examples.cn: 将军研究敌人的山地战术。

examples.en: She changed tactics and wrote to the editor instead.
examples.cn: 她改变了策略，转而写信给编辑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特启课」——特地为启动这件事开一节课，把策略讲清楚；这只是谐音联想，与希腊语词源无关。

root: 希腊语 tassein（排列）→ taktike（排列之术，尤指排兵）→ 拉丁语 tactica → 法语 tactique → 英语 tactic（策略；战术）。

sensesIntro.en: Tactic moves from the battlefield art of arranging troops to one planned move in any campaign, and finally to a move that only stalls.
sensesIntro.cn: tactic 从战场上排兵布阵之术，转到任何行动中一个计划好的动作，最后也可指单纯拖延的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand moving one chess piece to prepare the next move.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手挪动一枚棋子，为下一步做准备。

branches.en: One planned move toward a goal is the general sense.
branches.cn: 朝目标的一个计划动作是通用义项。

branches.en: Moving troops in battle is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 在战斗中调遣部队是最古老的义项。

branches.en: A move that only buys time is the weakened sense.
branches.cn: 只为争取时间的动作是弱化的义项。

branches.en: Both a battle move and a daily plan rely on arrangement.
branches.cn: 战斗动作与日常计划都依赖「安排」。

branches.en: A delay tactic is still a planned move, only a negative one.
branches.cn: 拖延策略仍是有计划的动作，只是性质消极。

intro.en: Tactic has a Greek arranging root, and English builds tactic words with noun, adjective, and person suffixes.
intro.cn: tactic 有希腊语「排列」词根，英语又用名词、形容词与指人后缀构成一批词。

latinIntro.en: Latin tactica comes from Greek taktike, both built on the verb tassein, to arrange.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tactica 来自希腊语 taktike，二者都建立在动词 tassein（排列）之上。

items.meaning: to arrange, to place in order
items.example: Tassein is the root behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: tassein 是整个词族的根源。

items.example: Taktike names the skill of ordering troops.
items.exampleCN: taktike 指排兵布阵的技艺。

items.example: Tactica brought the word into Latin.
items.exampleCN: tactica 把这个词带入拉丁语。

items.example: Tactic names a single move.
items.exampleCN: tactic 指单个动作。

items.meaning: the study of moves in battle
items.example: The plural tactics also names a subject.
items.exampleCN: 复数 tactics 也能指一门学科。

items.example: The suffix -al forms tactical.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 tactical。

items.example: Tactical describes a move in action.
items.exampleCN: tactical 描述行动中的做法。

items.example: The suffix -ian forms tactician.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ian 构成 tactician。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms tactically.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 tactically。

latinEntries.meaning: to arrange, to put in order

definition_zh: 触觉的；手感舒适的；（人）喜欢触摸的；有触感的
definition_en: connected with the sense of touch, especially in a way that feels pleasant when you touch something
core_image: 手指慢慢抚过布面，布料细密的纹路在指尖被读出来
scene: 盲文读本上，一排排凸起的小点排成密密的行列。Her fingers feel the tactile dot of each letter on the braille page.
sceneCN: 这里 tactile 是「触觉的」（第 1 个义项：与触感相关的）；句意：她的手指隔着盲文页面摸到每个字母的触觉点。

pos.zh: （材料、织物）手感舒适的；有质感的
喜欢触摸的；爱动手摸的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「触感、可触性」
由形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「在触觉上、通过触碰」，较少用
加 -ly 构成的副词形式，义为「以触觉的方式」，多为临时构词，不如 tactually 通用

senses.title: Related to the sense of touch
senses.definition: connected with the sense of touch, especially with information received through the skin and fingertips
senses.definitionCN: 与触觉有关的，尤指通过皮肤和指尖获得信息的
senses.example: Braille is a tactile writing system read with the fingers.
senses.exampleCN: 盲文是一种用手指阅读的触觉书写系统。
senses.why: Tactile comes from the Latin tangere, to touch, so it first names anything that belongs to the act of touching.
senses.whyCN: tactile 源自拉丁语 tangere（触摸），所以它首先指一切属于「触摸」这一动作的事物，是把触觉本身概念化。

senses.title: Pleasant to touch as a material quality
senses.definition: having a surface that feels good when touched, such as a soft or finely textured fabric
senses.definitionCN: 表面摸起来舒服的，如柔软或纹理细致的织物
senses.example: The wool blanket is warm and remarkably tactile.
senses.exampleCN: 这条羊毛毯很暖和，手感也格外好。
senses.why: If the sense of touch can be named, then a surface that pleases that sense takes the same word.
senses.whyCN: 既然触觉可以被命名，那么取悦触觉的表面自然也会被冠上同一个词，于是「触觉的」延伸为「摸起来舒服的、有质感的」。

senses.title: Describing a person who likes touching
senses.definition: describing a person who often touches others affectionately or needs to handle things to feel close to them
senses.definitionCN: 形容常亲昵地触碰他人，或必须亲手摸到东西才觉得亲近的人
senses.example: He is a tactile person who greets every friend with a hug.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个爱用身体接触表达的人，见朋友就拥抱。
senses.why: A person whose main way of knowing the world runs through the fingertips is described by the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 有些人的主要感知方式就是靠指尖去认识世界，于是这个词又用来形容这样的人，核心仍是「触摸」。

senses.title: Physical feedback from equipment
senses.definition: describing a control, screen, or device that gives physical feedback that the hand can feel, such as a click or a vibration
senses.definitionCN: 形容控制键、屏幕或设备能给出手可感知的物理反馈，如咔哒声或震动
senses.example: The camera has tactile buttons that click under your thumb.
senses.exampleCN: 这台相机的按钮带有触感，拇指按下去会发出咔哒声。
senses.why: Modern devices turn touch into a designed experience, so the adjective moves from the human sense to the hardware that imitates it.
senses.whyCN: 现代设备把触感变成了被设计出来的体验，形容词于是从人的感觉延伸到模仿这种感觉的硬件。

senses.title: Tangible enough to be touched
senses.definition: having a solid physical form that a hand can actually touch rather than only imagine
senses.definitionCN: 具有实体形态、手真的能摸到而不只是想象的
senses.example: The museum lets visitors handle tactile copies of the ancient pots.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆让参观者亲手触摸古代陶罐的仿制品。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word simply asserts that a thing can be touched at all, a meaning that design and art have renewed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层含义只是断言某物可以被摸到，今天设计与艺术领域又重新强调了这一层。

intro.en: Tactile comes from Latin tactilis, able to be touched, built on tactus, a touch, from tangere, to touch.
intro.cn: tactile 来自拉丁语 tactilis（可触摸的），词根为 tactus（触摸），源自动词 tangere（触摸）。

items.en: Tangere means to touch or to handle.
items.cn: tangere 意为触摸、接触。

items.en: Tactus, the past participle used as a noun, means a touch.
items.cn: tactus 是它的过去分词并作名词用，意为触摸。

items.en: Tactilis describes what can be touched or feels a certain way.
items.cn: tactilis 形容可以被触摸的东西，或摸起来某种感觉。

items.en: Scientific writing borrows tactilis for anatomy and the study of sensation.
items.cn: 十七世纪的科学写作借入 tactilis，用于解剖学与感觉研究。

items.en: English tactile first appears in learned medical and philosophical texts.
items.cn: 英语的 tactile 最早出现在学术性的医学与哲学文本中。

items.en: Modern English extends the word to fabric, product design, and digital feedback.
items.cn: 现代英语把该词扩展到织物、产品设计与数码反馈领域。

note.en: Tactile shares the tangere root with tact, contact, and tangent, and sits close to the broader synonyms of touch.
note.cn: tactile 与 tact、contact、tangent 共享 tangere 词根，并与更宽泛的一批「触摸」近义词相邻。

entries.definition: skill in dealing with people so as not to offend them
entries.definitionCN: 得体；善于与人打交道

entries.definition: the state of two things or people touching
entries.definitionCN: 接触；联系

entries.definition: a straight line that touches a curve at one point
entries.definitionCN: 切线；仅在一处相碰的直线

entries.definition: real and able to be felt by touch
entries.definitionCN: 有形的；可触知的；另见「可触摸」义项，但更常指「具体真实」

entries.definition: relating to the sense of touch, especially in technology
entries.definitionCN: 触觉的，技术语境常用，源自希腊语而非拉丁语

entries.definition: relating to touch as a sense, in psychology
entries.definitionCN: 触觉的，心理学或学术用法

normalIntro.en: Tactile keeps the hand in the word: it comes from the Latin verb for touching and still points at fingertips.
normalIntro.cn: tactile 把「手」留在词里：它来自拉丁语的「触摸」动词，至今仍指向指尖。

normal.en: Tactile, tact, and contact all go back to tangere, to touch.
normal.cn: tactile、tact、contact 都可追溯到 tangere（触摸）。

normal.en: Tactile sense is another name for the sense of touch.
normal.cn: tactile sense 就是触觉的另一种说法。

normal.en: A tactile learner needs to handle models instead of only listening.
normal.cn: 触觉型学习者需要亲手摸到模型，而不只是听讲。

normal.en: Tactile paving on a walkway is felt through the soles of the feet.
normal.cn: 人行道上的触觉铺面是靠脚底感觉到的。

normal.en: Compare tangible: tangible stresses that a thing is real, tactile stresses the sense itself.
normal.cn: 对比 tangible：tangible 强调东西真实存在，tactile 强调感觉本身。

abstract.en: Picture fingertips reading a row of raised dots in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象指尖在黑暗里读出一排凸起的小点。

abstract.en: Imagine a jumper so soft that customers rub it for a full minute.
abstract.cn: 想象一件软到顾客要摩挲整整一分钟的毛衣。

abstract.en: Think of a friend who hugs everyone long before they say a word.
abstract.cn: 想象一个朋友，还没开口就先张开双臂拥抱每个人。

examples.en: Good product design should be both visual and tactile.
examples.cn: 好的产品设计应当既好看又好摸。

examples.en: Birds use tactile signals when they preen one another.
examples.cn: 鸟类互相理羽时会传递触觉信号。

examples.en: The tactile quality of raw silk is what buyers look for first.
examples.cn: 买家最先看重的就是生丝的手感。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泰克太」——手指一「太」用力，就摸到了；把 tactile 读成伸手去摸的动作即可。这只是一种联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tangere（触摸）→ tactus（触摸）→ tactilis（可触摸的）→ 英语 tactile，核心义「与触摸相关」。

sensesIntro.en: Tactile starts from the sense of touch itself, then moves to materials that please it, to people who rely on it, to devices that imitate it, and finally back to things that can simply be touched.
sensesIntro.cn: tactile 从触觉本身出发，进而指取悦触觉的材质、依赖触觉的人、模仿触觉的设备，最后又回到能被触摸的实体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fingertip slowly tracing the grain of a piece of cloth.
core.cn: 核心意象：指尖慢慢划过一块布的纹理。

branches.en: The sense of touch sits closest to the root tangere.
branches.cn: 触觉这一层离词根 tangere 最近。

branches.en: A surface that pleases the hand grows out of the tactile sense.
branches.cn: 让手感到愉悦的表面，正是从触觉里长出来的。

branches.en: Some people put the fingertips before words in daily contact.
branches.cn: 有些人日常交往总是先用指尖而非语言。

branches.en: Buttons that click and pots you may hold both keep the word physical.
branches.cn: 会咔哒作响的按钮与可以上手的陶罐，都让这个词保持物理性。

branches.en: All three rest on the same skin and fingertip experience.
branches.cn: 三层都建立在同一份皮肤与指尖经验之上。

intro.en: Tactile is the Latin adjective of touching; around it gather tact, contact, tangible, and the older noun tactus.
intro.cn: tactile 是拉丁语中表示「触摸」的形容词，周围聚集着 tact、contact、tangible 以及更早的 tactus。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family of tangere includes tactus, the touch itself, tactilis, touchable, and tangere itself.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tangere 词族包括 tactus（触摸本身）、tactilis（可触摸的）和动词 tangere。

items.example: Tangere is the verb behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: tangere 是整个词族背后的动词。

items.meaning: a touch, the sense of touch
items.example: Tactus names the act and the sense.
items.exampleCN: tactus 同时指动作与感觉。

items.example: The suffix -ilis turns tactus into tactilis.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ilis 把 tactus 变成 tactilis。

items.example: Tactilis is the direct source of tactile.
items.exampleCN: tactilis 是 tactile 的直接来源。

items.example: Tactile keeps the Latin adjectival shape.
items.exampleCN: tactile 保留了拉丁语形容词的形态。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms tactility from tactile.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 由 tactile 构成 tactility。

items.example: Tactility describes how a material feels.
items.exampleCN: tactility 描述材料的触感。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms tactually and tactilely.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 tactually 与 tactilely。

items.example: Tactually is the standard adverb from the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: tactually 是由拉丁词干构成的常用副词。

items.example: Tact shifts the touch image from skin to manners.
items.exampleCN: tact 把「触摸」的比喻从皮肤移到了举止上。

definition_zh: 蝌蚪；引申指幼小阶段或尚在发育中的人
definition_en: the small swimming larva of a frog or toad, with a round head and a long tail but no legs at first
core_image: 池塘浅水里，一团黑色的小身体带着细长的尾巴来回摆动着
scene: 春末的小池塘里，密密麻麻的小蝌蚪贴着水面游动。Every spring the shallow pond fills with tadpoles.
sceneCN: 这里 tadpole 是「蝌蚪」（第 1 个义项：蛙或蟾蜍的幼体）；句意：每年春天，浅浅的池塘里都挤满了蝌蚪。

pos.zh: （比喻）幼小阶段；尚未成熟的人或事物

collocations.phrase: a tadpole turns into a frog

derivatives.zh: 构成 tadpole 的前半部分，本义为「小孩、小家伙」，与 pole 组合成「头部像小孩的双足动物」
蝌蚪的英语同义词，取自「头部加摇动的尾巴」的画面，与 tadpole 各自独立构成

senses.title: The larva of a frog or toad
senses.definition: the small dark larva that hatches from frog or toad spawn and swims about with a rounded head and a long tail
senses.definitionCN: 由蛙或蟾蜍的卵孵化出的深色小幼体，圆头长尾，在水中游动
senses.example: The children caught a tadpole in a jam jar.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们用果酱瓶捉到一只蝌蚪。
senses.why: The oldest name pictures the rounded head as a little child and the tail as a foot, so the larva was called a toad that walks on two.
senses.whyCN: 最早命名时把这圆圆的头看作一个小孩，把尾巴看作一只脚，于是蝌蚪被叫作「用两只脚站立的蟾蜍」，义项直接来自这个画面。

senses.title: The short legless early stage of growth
senses.definition: a stage in the life of an amphibian before legs grow and the body takes its adult shape
senses.definitionCN: 两栖动物长出腿、身体变成成体形态之前的阶段
senses.example: Wood frogs pass through the tadpole stage in about two months.
senses.exampleCN: 林蛙大约两个月就度过蝌蚪期。
senses.why: Because every frog and toad must pass through this form, the noun can also name that developing stage itself.
senses.whyCN: 因为每一只蛙都必须经过这个形态，所以这个词也可以直接指称这个「正在发育的形体阶段」。

senses.title: A person or thing still far from mature
senses.titleCN: （比喻）尚无成就的新手；幼小的雏形
senses.definition: a person, idea, or project that is still small and not fully formed, used in informal or figurative writing
senses.definitionCN: 指仍幼小、尚未成形的人、想法或计划，多用于非正式或比喻写作
senses.example: His brilliant idea was still a tadpole when the meeting began.
senses.exampleCN: 会议开始时，他那个绝妙的想法还只是个雏形。
senses.why: Since the tadpole looks nothing like the frog it becomes, the word can tease anything that is small now but will grow later.
senses.whyCN: 蝌蚪的模样与它日后的样子毫无相似之处，所以这个词也常被用来打趣那些现在很小、将来会长大的事物。

intro.en: Tadpole is an English compound of tad, a small child, and pole, a poorly understood element present from the fourteenth century form taddepol.
intro.cn: tadpole 是英语的合成词：前半 tad 意为小孩，后半 pole 来源存疑，这种写法在十四世纪的 taddepol 中已经存在。

items.en: Taddepol appears meaning the larva of a frog or toad.
items.cn: taddepol 出现，指蛙或蟾蜍的幼体。

items.en: Tad here means a small child, as in the old word for a toddler.
items.cn: 这里的 tad 意为「小孩」，与指刚学走路孩童的古老说法同源。

items.en: A popular explanation says the second part means a head, but this is not certain.
items.cn: 一种流行的解释认为后半部分意为「头」，但这并不确定，一般认为证据不足。

items.en: Others link the second part to poll, the head of an animal.
items.cn: 也有人认为后半部分与 poll（动物的头）有关，学界仍有争议。

items.en: The spelling settles into tadpole, with the compound no longer felt as two words.
items.cn: 拼写逐渐固定为 tadpole，人们不再把它看作两部分。

items.en: Modern dictionaries keep the head theory only as a traditional folk explanation.
items.cn: 现代词典只把「头部」一说作为传统的民间解释保留。

note.en: Tadpole belongs to a small family of native English frog words, and sits beside the amphibian life stages it passes through.
note.cn: tadpole 属于一小群英本土蛙类词汇，并与它经历的两栖动物生命阶段相邻。

entries.definition: a small child, and a little bit
entries.definitionCN: 小家伙；一点点，是 tadpole 的前半部分

entries.definition: an older English word for a tadpole
entries.definitionCN: 蝌蚪的旧式英语说法，由「头」与「摇摆」两部分构成

entries.definition: a student or lover of archery
entries.definitionCN: 射箭爱好者，只是拼写末尾相近，词源完全不同

entries.definition: the jelly like eggs of a frog in a pond
entries.definitionCN: 池塘中成团的蛙卵，是蝌蚪出现之前的样子

entries.definition: a young frog that has just lost its tail
entries.definitionCN: 刚失去尾巴的小蛙，是蝌蚪之后的阶段

entries.definition: a small amphibian with a long body and tail that lives in ponds
entries.definitionCN: 蝾螈，同样生活在水边的小型两栖动物

normalIntro.en: Tadpole is a picture carried inside a word: a little tad of a creature trailing a long tail.
normalIntro.cn: tadpole 把一幅画藏在了词里：一个小小的小家伙拖着一条长尾巴。

normal.en: Tad is an old word for a small child, and the front of tadpole keeps it.
normal.cn: tad 是小孩的旧称，tadpole 的前半部分正是它。

normal.en: Polliwog is the older or regional name that keeps the same picture.
normal.cn: polliwog 是更古老或地方性的说法，画面相同。

normal.en: A frogspawn mass turns into hundreds of tadpoles in a few days.
normal.cn: 一团蛙卵几天之内就会变成成百上千只蝌蚪。

normal.en: As its legs grow, a tadpole absorbs its own tail for food.
normal.cn: 长出腿的过程中，蝌蚪会吸收自己的尾巴当作养料。

normal.en: Compare froglet: a tadpole swims, a froglet hops and is nearly a frog.
normal.cn: 对比 froglet：蝌蚪在水里游，froglet 会跳、几乎已是青蛙。

abstract.en: Picture a wriggling comma made of black ink, darting along the pond bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象一个蠕动的黑色逗号，贴着池底到处窜。

abstract.en: Imagine counting the stages on a chalkboard: egg, tadpole, legs, frog.
abstract.cn: 想象在黑板上数阶段：卵、蝌蚪、长腿、青蛙。

abstract.en: Think of a start up shown on a slideshow as a tiny tadpole that will become a frog.
abstract.cn: 想象演讲里的初创公司被画成一只小蝌蚪，将来会变成青蛙。

examples.en: Tadpoles breathe initially with gills and later with lungs.
examples.cn: 蝌蚪最初用鳃呼吸，之后改用肺。

examples.en: A heron can swallow a whole clutch of tadpoles in one go.
examples.cn: 一只苍鹭一口就能吞下整窝蝌蚪。

examples.en: By June the tadpoles had grown back legs.
examples.cn: 到了六月，这些蝌蚪已经长出了后腿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「他的婆」——想想一位老奶奶在池塘边舀蝌蚪喂鸡。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语本土合成词：tad（小孩，约十四世纪）+ pole（来源存疑，一说指「头」）→ taddepol → tadpole，核心义「头部如小孩、带尾的幼体」。

sensesIntro.en: Tadpole names the larva itself, then the stage it lives through, and finally anything that starts out small and unfinished.
sensesIntro.cn: tadpole 先指蝌蚪本身，再指它所处的发育阶段，最后引申为任何起初幼小、尚未成形的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a black comma with a tail, swimming through the shallows of a pond.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个带尾巴的黑色逗号，在池塘浅水里游动。

branches.en: The swimming larva itself is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 游动的幼体是字面义。

branches.en: The whole period before the legs grow makes the stage sense.
branches.cn: 长出腿之前的整段时间构成阶段义。

branches.en: Anything that will grow far beyond its current shape echoes the figurative sense.
branches.cn: 任何日后会长得远超此刻模样的事物，都呼应比喻义。

branches.en: The creature and its stage share one spring in a single pond.
branches.cn: 这种生物与它的阶段共用同一个池塘里的同一个春天。

branches.en: Both senses depend on the gap between now and later.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖「现在」与「以后」之间的落差。

intro.en: Tadpole is built from two English elements rather than Latin ones: tad, a child, and the disputed pole.
intro.cn: tadpole 由两个英语成分构成，而非拉丁语成分：tad（小孩）与存疑的 pole。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor for tadpole; the native English compound has no Latin relatives.
latinIntro.cn: tadpole 没有拉丁语祖先，这个英语本土合成词也没有拉丁同族词。

items.example: Tad keeps only this child sense today.
items.exampleCN: tad 今天只保留了「小孩」这一含义。

items.meaning: the head of a person or animal
items.example: Poll is one candidate for the second part.
items.exampleCN: poll 是后半部分的一种可能来源。

items.meaningCN: tadpole 中含义不明的部分
items.example: Pole in tadpole is not the long piece of wood.
items.exampleCN: tadpole 里的 pole 并不是那根长木头。

items.example: Taddepol is the earliest recorded spelling.
items.exampleCN: taddepol 是文献中最早的拼写。

items.example: Tadpole generalises to any young form.
items.exampleCN: tadpole 可引申为任何幼小的形态。

items.example: Polliwog is the regional rival of tadpole.
items.exampleCN: polliwog 是 tadpole 的地方同义词。

items.example: Frog is the end of the tadpole story.
items.exampleCN: frog 是蝌蚪故事的去处。

items.meaning: related animal with the same larva
items.meaningCN: 蟾蜍与蛙共有同样的幼体
items.example: Toad and frog share the same word for the young.
items.exampleCN: 蟾蜍与蛙共用同一个词称呼幼体。

items.meaning: the eggs from which tadpoles hatch
items.example: Spawn is the beginning of the chain.
items.exampleCN: spawn 是这条生长链的起点。

definition_zh: 可触知地；具体地；确实地；显著地
definition_en: in a way that can be touched or clearly felt, or in a real and noticeable manner
core_image: 手指碰到一块木头的表面，能清楚地摸到它实实在在的棱角
scene: 项目评审会上，负责人没有讲口号，只把改进前后的数据摊在桌上。The results were tangibly better after the new process.
sceneCN: 这里 tangibly 是「显著地、实实在在地」（第 2 个义项：程度上明显可感）；句意：改用新流程后，结果实实在在地变好了。

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，义为「可触知的；有形的；明确的」，tangibly 正是它加副词词尾构成的形式
由 tangible 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「可触知性；具体性」
由 tangible 加 -ness 构成，义同 tangibility，但较少使用

senses.title: In a way that can be touched
senses.definition: so that something can be felt by the hand or seen to have real physical form
senses.definitionCN: 使某物能被手摸到，或看得出具有真实物理形态
senses.example: The sculpture stands tangibly within reach of every visitor.
senses.exampleCN: 这尊雕塑实实在在立在每位参观者伸手可及的地方。
senses.why: Tangibly is the adverb of tangible, from Latin tangere, to touch, so it first says that an action happens in a touchable way.
senses.whyCN: tangibly 是有形形容词的副词形式，源自拉丁语 tangere（触摸），所以它首先表示某事以「摸得到」的方式发生。

senses.title: To a degree that can clearly be felt
senses.definition: by an amount that is big enough to be seen, felt, or measured rather than only imagined
senses.definitionCN: 变化大到可以被看到、感觉到或测量出来，而不只是想象中的
senses.example: Living costs have risen tangibly since last winter.
senses.exampleCN: 自从去年冬天以来，生活成本明显上涨了。
senses.why: What the hand can feel, the whole person can verify, so the adverb stretches from skin contact to any change you can check.
senses.whyCN: 手能摸到的，整个人就能验证，所以副词从皮肤接触延伸到任何能被检验的变化，成为「明显可见」的强度修饰。

senses.title: In practical, concrete terms
senses.titleCN: 具体地；以实际成效的方式
senses.definition: in a way that produces real and measurable effects rather than only promises or explanations
senses.definitionCN: 以产生真实、可衡量的效果的方式，而非只停留在承诺或解释上
senses.example: The charity does not just raise awareness; it helps tangibly.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构不只是提高意识，还实实在在地提供帮助。
senses.why: If results can be felt, they can also be shown, so the adverb names proof by action instead of words.
senses.whyCN: 结果既然能被感觉到，也就能被证明出来，于是这个副词专指用行动而非言语来证明的「具体」。

intro.en: Tangibly is tangible plus the English adverb suffix -ly; tangible itself comes from Late Latin tangibilis, able to be touched.
intro.cn: tangibly 由 tangible 加英语副词词尾 -ly 构成；tangible 则来自晚期拉丁语 tangibilis（能被触摸的）。

items.en: Tangere means to touch or to take hold of.
items.cn: tangere 意为触摸、抓住。

items.en: Tangibilis, formed with the suffix -ibilis, means able to be touched.
items.cn: 加后缀 -ibilis 形成的 tangibilis 意为「能被触摸的」。

items.en: Scholastic Latin uses tangibilis to classify the objects of the senses.
items.cn: 经院学派的拉丁语用 tangibilis 来给感官对象分类。

items.en: English borrows tangible for things that can be felt.
items.cn: 英语借入 tangible，指可被摸到的东西。

items.en: The adverb tangibly is built with -ly from the adjective.
items.cn: 副词 tangibly 由形容词加 -ly 构成。

items.en: Finance and business speech extend it to assets and to clearly visible results.
items.cn: 金融与商业话语把它扩展到有形资产以及明显可见的成果。

note.en: Tangibly is the adverb built on tangible; its family runs from tangere through contact and tact, and its neighbours are the adverbs of clarity and reality.
note.cn: tangibly 是建立在 tangible 之上的副词；词族从 tangere 延伸到 contact、tact，近邻则是表示「明显」与「真实」的副词。

entries.definition: real enough to be touched or clearly felt
entries.definitionCN: 可触知的；有形的；明确的

entries.definition: connected with the sense of touch
entries.definitionCN: 触觉的；同出 tangere 词根

entries.definition: care not to hurt people by what you say
entries.definitionCN: 得体；圆融，来自同一「触摸」词根

entries.definition: in a way that can easily be seen
entries.definitionCN: 明显地；看得见地

entries.definition: so strongly that it seems you could touch it
entries.definitionCN: 强烈得几乎可以触摸到地

entries.definition: in clearly stated and practical terms
entries.definitionCN: 具体地；明确地

normalIntro.en: Tangibly says that a change is real enough for your hand to notice it; the word is built on the Latin verb for touching.
normalIntro.cn: tangibly 说的是某个变化真实到连手都能觉察；这个词建立在拉丁语的「触摸」动词之上。

normal.en: Tangibly and tangible share the root of tangere, to touch.
normal.cn: tangibly 与 tangible 共享 tangere（触摸）这个根。

normal.en: Tangible assets are things a company can touch; tangibly greater profits are things it can show.
normal.cn: tangible assets 指公司摸得到的资产；tangibly greater profits 指公司能拿出来展示的利润。

normal.en: To say something improved tangibly is to say the improvement can be checked.
normal.cn: 说某事 improved tangibly，就是说话里的改善能被检验。

normal.en: Tangibly closer means almost close enough to reach out and hold.
normal.cn: tangibly closer 的意思几乎就是近到伸手就能抱住。

normal.en: Compare abstractly: tangibly shows effects, abstractly talks about ideas.
normal.cn: 对比 abstractly：tangibly 展示效果，abstractly 谈论观念。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a wooden edge; the finger recognises the corner at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手搭在木桌边沿，手指一下子就认出了那个棱角。

abstract.en: Imagine the thermometer rising, and everyone in the room feeling it at once.
abstract.cn: 想象温度计的水银柱往上升，屋里每个人都立刻感觉到了。

abstract.en: Think of a promise compared with a receipt: the receipt is tangibly real.
abstract.cn: 想一下一句承诺和一张收据：收据才是实实在在的。

examples.en: Air quality improved tangibly after the factory closed.
examples.cn: 工厂关闭后，空气质量明显改善。

examples.en: The new coach made the players tangibly more confident.
examples.cn: 新教练让队员们明显更自信了。

examples.en: She could tangibly feel the heat of the stone wall.
examples.cn: 她能真切地摸到石墙的热度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「谈鸡不利」——谈判里空谈鸡肉的价格，不如去鸡笼里摸一摸，那样才具体。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tangere（触摸）→ 晚期拉丁语 tangibilis（可触摸的）→ 英语 tangible（有形的）→ tangible + -ly（副词）→ tangibly，核心义「能被摸到地、因此真切可见」。

sensesIntro.en: Tangibly first keeps the hand in view, then extends to any change strong enough to be felt, and finally to results that can be shown rather than promised.
sensesIntro.cn: tangibly 首先停留在「手能触摸」上，再延伸到任何强到可以被感知的变化，最后用来指能被展示而非只是被承诺的成果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fingertip finding a solid corner that is really there.
core.cn: 核心意象：指尖摸到一个真切存在的硬角。

branches.en: Touching an object is the narrowest, most physical sense.
branches.cn: 触摸物件是最狭窄、最物理的义项。

branches.en: A change large enough to feel grows from the same physical certainty.
branches.cn: 大到能被感觉到的变化，来自同一种物理上的确定感。

branches.en: Results that can be shown rather than argued complete the arc.
branches.cn: 可以摆出来而不是争辩出来的结果，完成了这一条语义弧线。

branches.en: Both rest on the body being able to verify what language claims.
branches.cn: 两者都依赖身体去证实语言所声称的东西。

branches.en: Measured gains and proven results feed one another.
branches.cn: 可量化的增长与经得起验证的成果彼此支撑。

intro.en: Tangibly is a small English machine: the Latin stem tang- plus -ible plus -ly, with contact and tact as cousins.
intro.cn: tangibly 像一台小小的构词机器：拉丁词干 tang- 加 -ible，再加 -ly，cousin 则有 contact 与 tact。

latinIntro.en: The Latin stem tang- gives tangere, to touch, tangibilis, touchable, and the past participle tactus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词干 tang- 衍生出 tangere（触摸）、tangibilis（可触摸的）以及过去分词 tactus。

items.example: Tangere is the verb at the centre of the family.
items.exampleCN: tangere 是这个词族的核心动词。

items.meaning: the touch stem found in derivatives
items.example: The stem tang- appears in tangible and tangent.
items.exampleCN: 词干 tang- 出现在 tangible 与 tangent 中。

items.example: The suffix -ible turns tangere into tangibilis.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ible 把 tangere 变成 tangibilis。

items.example: Tangibilis is the direct ancestor of tangible.
items.exampleCN: tangibilis 是 tangible 的直接祖先。

items.example: Tangible keeps the ability sense of the Latin suffix.
items.exampleCN: tangible 保留了拉丁语词尾的「能够」之意。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms tangibly from tangible.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 由 tangible 构成 tangibly。

items.meaning: in a touchable or clearly felt way
items.example: Tangibly is the adverb used of visible results.
items.exampleCN: tangibly 是用于可见成果的副词。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms tangibility.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 tangibility。

items.example: Tangibility measures how real an asset feels.
items.exampleCN: tangibility 衡量某项资产有多实在。

items.example: Contact carries the same con- plus tang- build.
items.exampleCN: contact 同样由 con- 加 tang- 构成。

items.example: Tactile shares the past participle tactus.
items.exampleCN: tactile 共享过去分词 tactus。

definition_zh: 油轮；油槽车；运输液体的罐式船或车；空中加油机
definition_en: a large ship, vehicle, or aircraft built to carry liquid or gas in a tank
core_image: 一艘船体里塞满巨大钢罐的船，罐里盛着原油
scene: 港口的巨型油轮按顺序把原油输进管道的网络。The giant tanker pulses crude oil into a network of pipes at the port.
sceneCN: 这里 tanker 是「油轮」（第 1 个义项：运输原油的大型船只）；句意：港口的巨型油轮把原油输送进管道的网络。

pos.zh: 油轮；油槽车；罐式运输工具

derivatives.zh: 基础词，指储存液体或气体的大容器「罐、箱、槽」；加 -er 构成 tanker
由 tank「罐、油箱」加后缀 -ful（满的量）构成，义为「一箱、一罐的量」
由动词 tank 加 -ing 构成，义为「罐装、注入罐中」，与运输用法相邻

senses.title: A ship that carries oil in tanks
senses.definition: a large ocean-going ship whose hull is fitted with tanks for crude oil or fuel
senses.definitionCN: 船体内装有油罐、用于运载原油或燃油的大型远洋船舶
senses.example: The tanker docked at the terminal before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 油轮在天亮前靠泊在码头。
senses.why: Ship names like coaster, tanker, schooner let the -er suffix name a vessel by its cargo or type.
senses.whyCN: 像 coaster、schooner 这样的船名也用 -er 结尾，所以给船起名时 -er 指「装载某类货物的船」，油轮就是「以罐装油为货的船」。

senses.title: A road vehicle with a cylindrical tank
senses.definition: a lorries or truck with a large rounded tank on its chassis for carrying petrol, milk, or other liquids
senses.definitionCN: 底盘上装有大型圆罐、用于运输汽油、牛奶等液体的货车
senses.example: A milk tanker pulled up beside the dairy gate.
senses.exampleCN: 一辆牛奶罐车停在奶场大门边。
senses.why: The same tank idea moves onto wheels, so the suffix simply swaps a ship for a truck.
senses.whyCN: 「罐装运输」的想法从船上移到车轮上，后缀不变，只是把船换成了货车。

senses.title: An aircraft that refuels others in flight
senses.definition: a military aircraft carrying fuel and passing it to other aircraft during flight
senses.definitionCN: 携带燃油并在飞行途中向其他飞机输送燃料的军用飞机
senses.example: The fighters stayed aloft thanks to a tanker on call.
senses.exampleCN: 多亏有一架空中加油机随时待命，战斗机才一直在空中巡航。
senses.why: Air tankers turn the cargo tank into an airborne fuel station, the third stage of the same image.
senses.whyCN: 空中加油机把货舱里的油罐变成空中的加油站，是同一意象发展的第三步：罐成了移动补给站。

senses.title: A tanker load as a unit of trade
senses.definition: the full cargo of a tanker, used to count oil or liquid goods in trading
senses.definitionCN: 一整船或整罐的液货量，贸易中用来计量石油等液体货物
senses.example: They agreed on the price for each tanker.
senses.exampleCN: 他们就每船石油的价格达成了协议。
senses.why: Container as a metonym for cargo spread to tanker, so the vessel itself became a counting word.
senses.whyCN: container 从货物容器引申为计量单位，同理 tanker 也从船本身引申为「一整船的量」这样的计量名词。

senses.title: A tanker as a risk and a symbol
senses.titleCN: 油轮（象征污染与航运业）
senses.definition: a tanker considered as a source of spills, pollution, shipping costs, or geopolitical power
senses.definitionCN: 从泄漏、污染、航运成本或地缘政治影响力角度谈论的油轮
senses.example: Every tanker leaving the strait makes the whole area vulnerable to pollution.
senses.exampleCN: 每一艘驶出海峡的油轮都让整个地区面临被污染的风险。
senses.why: Because a tanker carries so much liquid, it became a figure for risk and for the oil trade itself.
senses.whyCN: 因为油轮一次装运的液体极多，它自然成为风险与石油贸易本身的象征：谈油轮，就是谈泄漏风险与能源命脉。

senses.title: The verb sense of carting liquid around
senses.definition: to transport liquid by means of a tanker or tank vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 用油轮或罐车来运输液体
senses.example: The oil is tankered south along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 石油沿海岸线用罐车向南运。
senses.why: English readily turns nouns into verbs, so the vessel becomes the action of hauling liquid in one.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用名词作动词，于是「用油轮运」成了动作义：船名转化为搬运液体的动作。

intro.en: Tanker is the noun tank plus the agent suffix -er, first recorded in English in the nineteenth century for a ship carrying liquids in tanks.
intro.cn: tanker 是名词 tank 加施事后缀 -er 构成的，英文最初在一八六零年代使用，指用罐舱运输液体的船。

items.en: Tanca or stanca names a water tank or pool in medieval Latin records.
items.cn: 中古拉丁语记录中 tanca 或 stanca 指水池、大水槽。

items.en: Tanc or tank carries the word from southern French into English.
items.cn: 普罗旺斯语与古法语 tanc 把这个词传入英语。

items.en: Tank appears in English first for a pool or large receptacle for liquid.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语 tank 先指水池或储液的大容器。

items.en: Tanker is coined for a ship whose tanks hold oil in bulk.
items.cn: 十九世纪造出 tanker，专指舱内有罐体、可整批运油的船。

items.en: Tanker extends to road vehicles and later to aircraft.
items.cn: 二十世纪初 tanker 扩展到公路罐车，后来又扩展到飞机。

items.en: Modern English uses tanker for ships, lorries, and air refuelling aircraft.
items.cn: 现代英语 tanker 兼指油轮、罐车与空中加油机。

note.en: Tanker sits in the tank family, with tank, tankful, and tanking, and near ship and vehicle words in meaning.
note.cn: tanker 属于 tank 词族，与 tank、tankful、tanking 同源，意义上也与轮船、车辆类词相邻。

entries.definition: a large container for liquid or gas
entries.definitionCN: 储液或储气的大容器；tanker 的基础词

entries.definition: a large drinking mug with a handle, usually for beer
entries.definitionCN: 带柄的大啤酒杯；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a straight line that touches a curve at one point
entries.definitionCN: 切线；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a truck fitted with a tank for liquids
entries.definitionCN: 罐式货车

entries.definition: the act of filling or storing in a tank
entries.definitionCN: 罐装；注入罐中

entries.definition: a ship built to carry goods packed in steel boxes
entries.definitionCN: 集装箱船：运箱子而非装罐子的货船

entries.definition: a large ship or aircraft that carries goods
entries.definitionCN: 货船；货运飞机

entries.definition: a ship that carries loose dry cargo such as grain or coal
entries.definitionCN: 散货船：运粮食、煤炭等干散货，与运液体的油轮相对

entries.definition: a large road vehicle for carrying goods
entries.definitionCN: 卡车；货车（英式说法）

normalIntro.en: Tanker is the tank word wearing the -er suffix: whatever carries a tank is a tanker.
normalIntro.cn: tanker 就是 tank 加上 -er：凡是带着罐子跑的东西，都可以叫 tanker。

normal.en: oil tanker packs crude into giant holds.
normal.cn: oil tanker 是装满原油的巨轮，最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Tanker and tank share the t-a-n-k letters.
normal.cn: tanker 与 tank 共享 t-a-n-k 四个字母，记住词根就能记住全部。

normal.en: A fleet of tankers means many of these ships sailing together.
normal.cn: a fleet of tankers 指一整支油轮船队。

normal.en: Tanker spill is the phrase used in news about oil pollution.
normal.cn: tanker spill 是新闻报道石油污染时的固定说法。

normal.en: Compare tank with fire engine: one holds water for fighting fires on the spot.
normal.cn: 对比消防用的水罐车：同样是罐，却服务于灭火，可以借此体会「罐加车」的构词逻辑。

abstract.en: See the sea as a moving storage yard full of tanks.
abstract.cn: 把大海想象成一座漂动的仓库，甲板下全是大罐子。

abstract.en: Imagine a long tub rolling along a dusty road.
abstract.cn: 想象一只长长的浴缸在尘土飞扬的公路上滚过。

abstract.en: Picture a plane passing a hose down to a thirsty jet.
abstract.cn: 想象一架飞机垂下油管，给另一架飞机喂油。

examples.en: An oil tanker blocked the narrow channel for almost a week.
examples.cn: 一艘油轮将近一个星期堵住了狭窄的航道。

examples.en: The milk tankers arrive at the farm before the cows are milked.
examples.cn: 牛奶罐车在挤奶之前就到了农场。

examples.en: Three tankers were sent to refuel the patrol aircraft.
examples.cn: 派出了三架加油机为巡逻机补充燃油。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坦克」——tanker 开头听起来像「坦克」，一艘装满油的坦克在海上开，就是油轮；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 tank（罐、水池，十七世纪借自普罗旺斯语或古法语，最终出自中古拉丁语 tanca），再加 -er 后缀构成 tanker，核心义「装罐运货的船」；词形来源不确定，存疑。

sensesIntro.en: The core image of a steel tank full of oil first gives the ship, then the road truck, then the airborne fuel stop, and finally counting, symbolic, and verb uses.
sensesIntro.cn: 「钢罐装满油」的核心意象，先长出油轮，再长出罐车、空中加油机，最后扩展到计量、象征与动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: steel tanks sealed inside a moving hull.
core.cn: 核心意象：钢罐被锁在移动的船体里。

branches.en: Ship, truck, and aircraft are the three physical homes of the tank.
branches.cn: 油轮、罐车与加油机是罐子的三个物理居所。

branches.en: The vessel becomes a counting unit in oil trading.
branches.cn: 船本身成了石油交易中的计量单位。

branches.en: The road tanker and its verb sense show cargo moving on land.
branches.cn: 罐车及其动词义说明液货在陆地上流动。

branches.en: In the air the tanker works as a fuel station.
branches.cn: 在空中，加油机就是一座流动的加油站。

branches.en: The tanker as a symbol of pollution grows straight out of the oil ship.
branches.cn: 油轮作为污染象征，直接由运油船这一形象引申而来。

intro.en: Tanker is built from the noun tank with the agent suffix -er, and the tank family also gives tankful and tanking.
intro.cn: tanker 由名词 tank 加施事后缀 -er 构成，tank 词族还包括 tankful 与 tanking。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer behind tank is medieval Latin tanca, a pool or receptacle, itself of uncertain origin.
latinIntro.cn: tank 背后的拉丁层是中古拉丁语 tanca（水池、容器），其源头本身存疑。

items.example: Tank is the base noun for tanker.
items.exampleCN: tank 是 tanker 的基础名词。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does or holds
items.meaningCN: 表示执行动作或承载事物的人或物
items.example: The suffix -er turns tank into tanker.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 把 tank 变成 tanker。

items.meaning: a ship or vehicle that carries liquids
items.example: Tanker names any liquid carrier.
items.exampleCN: tanker 泛指任何液体运输工具。

items.example: Oil tanker is the most common compound.
items.exampleCN: oil tanker 是最常见的复合词。

items.example: The suffix -ful forms tankful.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ful 构成 tankful。

items.meaning: as much as a tank holds
items.example: Tankful means a full tank.
items.exampleCN: tankful 表示满满一箱。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作的名词化词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms tanking.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 tanking。

items.meaning: filling or storing in a tank
items.example: Tanking describes the storing action.
items.exampleCN: tanking 描述储存的动作。

items.meaning: a group of tanks for storing fuel
items.example: Tank farm is the place where tanks cluster.
items.exampleCN: tank farm 是罐子聚集的油库。

derivatives.zh: 基础词，储液大容器
tank 加 -ful 构成，一箱的量

definition_zh: 单宁；鞣酸（使皮革鞣制、令茶酒发涩的植物多酚）；树皮中的鞣料；涩味本身
definition_en: a family of bitter plant compounds that tan leather, give tea and red wine an astringent taste, and darken certain surfaces
core_image: 泡着橡树皮的染缸，褐色汁液正在收紧生皮，皮革变硬
scene: 酿酒师摇了摇酒杯，葡萄酒的涩味让嘴唇微微收紧。The winemaker swirled the glass and felt his lips tighten from the tannin in the wine.
sceneCN: 这里 tannin 是「单宁」（第 1 个义项：使酒发涩的植物多酚）；句意：酿酒师转了转酒杯，感觉到酒中的单宁让嘴唇收紧。

derivatives.zh: 由 tannin 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为「单宁的；含单宁的；发涩的」
基础词，义为「鞣（皮）」；单宁一词正由鞣皮的 tannum 而来
由 tan「鞣皮」加 -ery（场所）构成，义为「制革厂」
由 tannin 词干加 -ate 构成，指单宁与金属或碱形成的盐类

senses.title: Bitter plant compounds that give astringency
senses.definition: a group of bitter, astringent plant polyphenols that make the mouth feel dry and puckered
senses.definitionCN: 一类味苦、收敛性强的植物多酚，使口腔感到干涩、发紧
senses.example: Strong black tea can be bitter because of tannin.
senses.exampleCN: 浓红茶因含有单宁而发苦。
senses.why: The chemical class takes its name from its leather-tanning power, and the drying feel is the same grip on the tongue.
senses.whyCN: 这类化学物质因能鞣制皮革而得名，而「让口腔发干发紧」的感觉，正是它对舌头与蛋白质那股收拢力在味觉上的翻版。

senses.title: The tanning agent in bark and wood
senses.definition: the natural substance in oak bark and other plant matter that tanners use to turn raw hides into leather
senses.definitionCN: 橡树皮及其他植物材料中的天然鞣料，制革者用它把生皮变成皮革
senses.example: The old tannery still soaks hides in tannin from oak bark.
senses.exampleCN: 那家老制革厂至今仍用橡树皮浸出的单宁鞣制皮革。
senses.why: This is the original use: tannin binds with hide proteins, so the word and the craft share one history.
senses.whyCN: 这是最原始的用途：单宁与皮中的蛋白质结合使皮革致密，因此这个词与鞣皮这门手艺同源同根。

senses.title: The drying grip felt in the mouth
senses.definition: the dry, rough sensation in the mouth that comes from eating or drinking something rich in tannins
senses.definitionCN: 吃下或喝下富含单宁的东西时，口腔里出现的干涩粗糙之感
senses.example: The red wine left a rough tannin on my tongue.
senses.exampleCN: 那杯红酒在我舌头上留下了一股粗涩的单宁感。
senses.why: The compound name shifts to the sensation it produces, a classic transfer from substance to effect.
senses.whyCN: 从物质名称转移到它造成的感觉，这是「以物代感」的常见引申：单宁让蛋白收紧，紧张感就成了「涩」。

senses.title: A wine-tasting descriptor
senses.definition: the quality and structure that tannins give red wine, described as soft, firm, grippy, or rough
senses.definitionCN: 单宁给红葡萄酒带来的质地与骨架，被描述为柔和、紧实、有抓口或粗涩
senses.example: The tannins in this cabernet are firm, so the wine needs more time in the cellar.
senses.exampleCN: 这瓶赤霞珠的单宁紧实，所以还需要在酒窖里多放些时候。
senses.why: Sommeliers turned the chemical into a structured vocabulary for judging how long a wine can age.
senses.whyCN: 品酒师把化学物质变成一套有结构的评语，用来判断酒能陈放多久，单宁于是成了「酒的骨架」的代名词。

senses.title: A stain that darkens surfaces
senses.definition: the brownish mark left on wood, fabric, stone, or concrete by tannins, often reaction stains rather than dust
senses.definitionCN: 单宁在木头、织物、石材或混凝土上留下的褐色痕迹，多是化学反应而非灰尘污渍
senses.example: Water plus tannin left a dark ring on the oak table.
senses.exampleCN: 水与单宁在橡木桌上留下了一圈深色痕迹。
senses.why: Because tannin binds with iron and other minerals, it leaves a chemically fixed dark stain that ordinary soaps ignore.
senses.whyCN: 单宁会与铁等离子结合，形成化学生成的深色固定污渍，普通肥皂根本洗不掉，所以它会跑到「污渍」义上。

senses.title: A protector against herbivores
senses.definition: tannins understood in ecology as chemical defences that make leaves unpalatable and bind gut proteins of insects
senses.definitionCN: 生态学视角下的单宁：让叶子难吃、并黏住昆虫肠道蛋白的化学防御物
senses.example: Oak leaves carry tannin as a quiet defence against insects.
senses.exampleCN: 橡树叶里的单宁是一种无声的防虫手段。
senses.why: The protein-binding trait that preserves leather also disrupts digestion, so the same molecule becomes a shield.
senses.whyCN: 能保住皮革的「黏蛋白」本领，同时也破坏昆虫的消化，同一分子于是变成植物无声的护盾。

intro.en: Tannin is formed from English tan, to convert hide into leather, plus the chemical suffix -in, echoing the French chemists who named the substance.
intro.cn: tannin 由英语 tan（鞣皮）加化学后缀 -in 构成，呼应法国化学家为这种物质命名时的用词。

items.en: A reconstructed Germanic root lies behind the sense of an oak tree or its bark.
items.cn: 一般认为可上溯到日耳曼语的重构词根，与橡树及其树皮相关。

items.en: Tann appears early for oak and its bark.
items.cn: 古英语 tann 早期指橡树及树皮。

items.en: Medieval Latin tannum names crushed oak bark used in tanning.
items.cn: 中古拉丁语 tannum 指制革用的碎橡树皮。

items.en: Tan or taner means crushed oak bark, and the verb tan appears.
items.cn: 古法语 tan 或 taner 指碎橡树皮，并出现了动词「鞣皮」。

items.en: Chemists isolate the active acid and name it tannin.
items.cn: 十九世纪化学家分离出有效成分，并将其命名为 tannin。

items.en: Tannin becomes everyday vocabulary for tea, wine, and plant science.
items.cn: 现代英语中 tannin 成为茶、酒与植物科学的日常词汇。

note.en: Tannin belongs to the tan family, near tannic and tannery, and in meaning sits close to astringent, polyphenol, and the chemistry of tea and wine.
note.cn: tannin 属于 tan 词族，与 tannic、tannery 相邻，意义上与涩味、多酚及茶酒化学相关。

entries.definition: containing tannin and tasting harsh or drying
entries.definitionCN: 含单宁的；发涩的

entries.definition: to convert animal hide into leather, or a brown colour
entries.definitionCN: 鞣制皮革；也指棕褐色

entries.definition: a place where hides are tanned
entries.definitionCN: 制革厂

entries.definition: a Jewish religious teacher of the first two centuries
entries.definitionCN: 犹太教早期经师；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a salt formed from tannic acid
entries.definitionCN: 单宁酸盐

entries.definition: causing a dry, bitter feeling in the mouth
entries.definitionCN: 收敛的；令人发涩的

entries.definition: a class of plant compounds that includes tannins
entries.definitionCN: 多酚：单宁所属的化学大类

entries.definition: another grape compound studied in red wine, very different from tannin
entries.definitionCN: 白藜芦醇：同为葡萄中的化合物，但与单宁不同

entries.definition: the basic aromatic compound behind the -ol ending in polyphenol
entries.definitionCN: 苯酚；多酚之名的词尾来源

normalIntro.en: Tannin is tan plus -in: the thing that does the tanning.
normalIntro.cn: tannin 就是 tan 加 -in：会「鞣」皮的那种物质。

normal.en: Tan a hide with bark, and the agent is tannin.
normal.cn: 用树皮鞣皮，起作用的东西就叫 tannin。

normal.en: Tannic describes anything full of tannin.
normal.cn: tannic 描述含单宁的东西，比如 tannic tea。

normal.en: Tannery is where the tanning happens.
normal.cn: tannery 是制革厂，是鞣皮的场所。

normal.en: High in tannin is the wine-tasting phrase for dryness.
normal.cn: high in tannin 是品酒时形容「干涩」的说法。

normal.en: The suffix -in marks chemical substances, as in insulin and caffeine.
normal.cn: 后缀 -in 多用来标记化学物质，如胰岛素、咖啡因，所以 tannin 也是一类化合物的名字。

abstract.en: Feel your whole mouth shrinking around a cup of strong tea.
abstract.cn: 想象含下一口浓茶，整个口腔被收得紧紧的。

abstract.en: See a vat of brown liquid pulling a raw hide tight.
abstract.cn: 看见一小桶褐色汁液把一张生皮绷得发紧。

abstract.en: Think of a sponge inside the mouth squeezing out every drop of wetness.
abstract.cn: 想象嘴里塞了一块海绵，把水分全吸走，留下涩涩的干。

examples.en: Oak bark was once the main source of tannin for leather makers.
examples.cn: 橡树皮曾是皮革匠获取单宁的主要来源。

examples.en: Red wines with soft tannins are ready to drink sooner.
examples.cn: 单宁柔和的红酒可以更早饮用。

examples.en: Soaking the beans removes much of their tannin.
examples.cn: 浸泡豆子可以去掉其中很大一部分单宁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「单宁」——这两个汉字读起来就是一个很「单」薄的「宁」静味道：喝口浓茶嘴里发紧；中文译名只是音译，并非词源。

root: 英语 tan（鞣皮）加化学后缀 -in 构成 tannin；tan 来自古法语 tan 与制革用中古拉丁语 tannum，指碎橡树皮，向上可追溯到与橡树有关的日耳曼语词根，重构形式存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Tannin starts as the compound that tans hide, then shifts to the drying taste it causes, then to the wine descriptor, the stain, and the ecological defence.
sensesIntro.cn: tannin 先指能鞣皮的化合物，再指它带来的干涩口感，然后延伸出品酒评语、污渍与植物防御等义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brown vat of bark liquor pulling a raw hide tight.
core.cn: 核心意象：褐色树皮汁把一张生皮绷得发紧。

branches.en: The plant substance and the tanning craft are the same history.
branches.cn: 植物中的物质与鞣皮手艺来自同一段历史。

branches.en: The compound name slides into the sensation it produces.
branches.cn: 化合物之名滑向它造成的口感。

branches.en: Taste becomes a professional tool for judging wine.
branches.cn: 口感进一步成为评价葡萄酒的专业工具。

branches.en: Protein binding explains both the leather and the brown stain.
branches.cn: 结合蛋白质的原理同时解释了鞣革与褐色污渍。

branches.en: The chemical defence reading grows from the same protein grip.
branches.cn: 生态学意义上的化学防御同样源于这种「抓住蛋白」的能力。

intro.en: Tannin is tan plus the chemical suffix -in, and the tan family supplies tannic, tannery, and tannate.
intro.cn: tannin 是 tan 加化学后缀 -in，tan 词族还提供 tannic、tannery 与 tannate。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is medieval Latin tannum, crushed oak bark used by tanners.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是中古拉丁语 tannum，即制革者使用的碎橡树皮。
