definition_zh: 撩拨；以可望而不可即之物逗引；挑逗食欲或好奇心；折磨式地诱惑
definition_en: to tease someone by showing or offering something desirable that they cannot have, or by promising it and then withholding it
core_image: 一挂水果悬在嘴边，一伸手就被拉开，永远差一点
scene: 面包房里飘出甜香，隔着玻璃柜挑起了一个人的食欲。The smell from the bakery window tantalized him through the glass cabinet.
sceneCN: 这里 tantalize 是「撩拨食欲」（第 2 个义项：挑动食欲）；句意：面包房橱窗里飘出的香味透过玻璃拨动他的食欲。

pos.zh: 逗引；挑逗；使可望而不可即

collocations.zh: 令人向往却又难以实现的前景

derivatives.zh: 由 tantalize 加 -ing 构成的形容词，义为「撩人的；诱人的；吊胃口的」
tantalizing 加 -ly 构成，义为「诱人地；让人可望而不可即地」
由 tantalize 加 -ation 构成，义为「挑逗、撩拨的行为或状态」
由 tantalize 加 -er 构成，义为「撩拨者；令人心动的东西」

senses.title: To hold something desirable just out of reach
senses.definition: to show someone something they badly want and then keep it just out of their reach
senses.definitionCN: 把人极想要的东西摆到他面前，却又让它始终够不着
senses.example: The shop tantalized her with a dress she could not afford.
senses.exampleCN: 商店用一条她买不起的裙子吊她的胃口。
senses.why: Tantalus in the Greek myth reached for food and water that always drew back, so the verb is built on that frustration.
senses.whyCN: 希腊神话中的坦塔洛斯每次伸手，食物和清水都会退开，这个动词正是由那份求而不得的挫败感造出来的。

senses.title: To stimulate appetite or desire with a hint
senses.definition: to arouse hunger, curiosity, or desire by a smell, a sample, or a taste of what is to come
senses.definitionCN: 用气味、样品或一点预告勾出人的饥饿、好奇或欲望
senses.example: A warm smell of bread tantalized everyone on the street.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵温热的麦香撩动着街上所有人的鼻子。
senses.why: When what is withheld is only partial, the same tease becomes a licence to desire rather than to suffer.
senses.whyCN: 当被扣住的东西只是「一部分」时，同样的逗引就从折磨变成勾起欲望：给一点，让你更想要更多。

senses.title: To tempt and then frustrate
senses.titleCN: 许诺又反悔；折磨式地吊着
senses.definition: to raise hopes of a reward or rescue and then deliberately delay or withdraw it
senses.definitionCN: 先让人以为有奖励或救援，再故意拖延或收回
senses.example: The report kept tantalizing readers with promises of proof it never gave.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报告不断用「即将给出证据」的承诺吊着读者，却始终没有给出。
senses.why: The myth ends in cruel denial, so the word keeps a punitive shade when a hopeful sign is withdrawn.
senses.whyCN: 神话以残忍的拒绝收场，因此当希望被亲手收回时，这个词仍带着「惩罚」的味道：先给你看，再让你落空。

senses.title: To tease in a playful or sexual way
senses.definition: to flirt with someone by giving attention and then withdrawing it
senses.definitionCN: 通过给予关注又收回关注来与某人调情
senses.example: He loved to tantalize her with quick glances and then turn away.
senses.exampleCN: 他喜欢用匆匆一瞥挑逗她，然后转过身去。
senses.why: Because the tease depends on approach and retreat, it drifts easily into the language of romance.
senses.whyCN: 挑逗的本质就是「靠近又退开」，所以这个词自然而然地滑向恋爱调情的用法。

senses.title: To be excitingly promising without fulfilment
senses.definition: describing a sign of something wonderful that hints at far more than it delivers
senses.definitionCN: 形容某种美好迹象暗示了远比它实际给予的更多
senses.example: A tantalizing glimpse of the finished room appeared in the trailer.
senses.exampleCN: 预告片里露出一瞥装修完成的房间，令人心驰神往。
senses.why: The adjective form shifted the focus from a person being teased to the thing that does the teasing.
senses.whyCN: 形容词用法把焦点从「被逗引的人」移到「逗引人的事物」上：是那个东西本身令人神往，哪怕它最终什么也没兑现。

senses.title: To repeatedly provoke hope in order to bait
senses.definition: to use offers as bait, keeping a person or animal pursuing what is always moved forward
senses.definitionCN: 把许诺当作诱饵，让人或动物一直追逐一个总被挪到前面去的东西
senses.example: The trappers tantalize the foxes with meat hung on a long pole.
senses.exampleCN: 猎人们用挂在长杆上的肉引诱狐狸。
senses.why: The bait dangles ahead exactly as the fruit dangled for Tantalus, so the word can describe deliberate luring.
senses.whyCN: 诱饵悬在前方，犹如那串悬在坦塔洛斯头顶的果子，所以这个词也可以指刻意设局引诱。

intro.en: Tantalize is coined in English from Tantalus, the Greek mythic king whose punishment was fruit and water that always withdrew.
intro.cn: tantalize 由希腊神话中的坦塔洛斯（Tantalus）之名加 -ize 造出，他的惩罚是永远够不到的果实与清水。

items.en: Tantalos is the king punished in the underworld of Greek myth.
items.cn: 古希腊神话中，坦塔洛斯是一位在地府受罚的国王。

items.en: Latin Tantalus names the same mythic figure and gives the stem.
items.cn: 拉丁语 Tantalus 指同一位神话人物，并提供了词干。

items.en: English writers first use tantalize for someone who tantalizes like Tantalus.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语作者首次用 tantalize 形容「像坦塔洛斯那样吊人」的人。

items.en: Tantalizing spreads to describe tempting prospects in general.
items.cn: 十七世纪 tantalizing 已扩展到泛指诱人却难兑现的前景。

items.en: The spelling tantalize and the British tantalise both settle in.
items.cn: 十八至十九世纪，英式拼写 tantalise 与美式拼写 tantalize 同时定型。

items.en: Modern English uses tantalizing for smells, previews, and unattainable offers.
items.cn: 现代英语中，tantalizing 常用在气味、预告与求之不得的诱惑上。

note.en: Tantalize is a myth-made verb of teasing, close to tempt and lure but with a built-in refusal, and shares spelling only with words like tantalum.
note.cn: tantalize 是由神话造出的「逗引」动词，与 tempt、lure 相近但自带「不给」这一层，与 tantalum 等词只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: a rare grey metal named after Tantalus for its chemical resistance
entries.definitionCN: 一种稀有灰色金属，因其耐腐蚀而得名于坦塔洛斯（但只是拼写相近）

entries.definition: so interesting or attractive that it is hard to resist
entries.definitionCN: 撩人的；诱人的

entries.definition: in a way that attracts but does not satisfy
entries.definitionCN: 诱人地；曾让人可望而不可即地

entries.definition: the British spelling of the same verb
entries.definitionCN: 同一动词的英式拼写

entries.definition: a person or thing that teases with what cannot be had
entries.definitionCN: 撩拨者；吊人胃口的事物

entries.definition: to make fun of someone playfully
entries.definitionCN: 逗弄；取笑

entries.definition: to make someone want to do something they may regret
entries.definitionCN: 诱惑；怂恿

entries.definition: to attract someone or something by offering a reward
entries.definitionCN: 引诱；投饵吸引

entries.definition: to prevent something from succeeding, the reverse of a tantalizing offer
entries.definitionCN: 挫败；阻挠：与「吊胃口」的留白相反

normalIntro.en: Tantalize is Tantalus plus -ize: to make someone feel exactly what Tantalus felt forever.
normalIntro.cn: tantalize 就是 Tantalus 加 -ize：让别人尝一尝坦塔洛斯永远在尝的那种滋味。

normal.en: Tantalus stands in water and fruit, yet both retreat.
normal.cn: 坦塔洛斯站在水里、头上悬着果子，可是水和果子都会退开。

normal.en: Tantalizing glimpse is a phrase for a preview that gives away too little.
normal.cn: tantalizing glimpse 指给得太少的「惊鸿一瞥」。

normal.en: Tempt means to offer; tantalize means to offer and then hold back.
normal.cn: tempt 是「给出诱惑」，tantalize 是「给了又收回」，区别就在于那一下收手。

normal.en: Tantalize takes -ize, and the British form is tantalise.
normal.cn: tantalize 用 -ize 词尾，英式拼法写作 tantalise。

normal.en: Tantalum, the metal, borrows the name but not the meaning.
normal.cn: 金属 tantalum 借了同一个名字，却没有「吊胃口」的意思。

abstract.en: Watch a plate of hot food slide past your eyes and come back empty.
abstract.cn: 看着一盘热菜从眼前滑过，转一圈回来后已经空了。

abstract.en: Smell fresh bread through a window that will not open.
abstract.cn: 闻着新鲜面包的香气，却推不开那扇窗。

abstract.en: See a treasure chest that the sand pulls away each time you reach.
abstract.cn: 看见一只宝箱，每次伸手，沙就把它拖远一点。

examples.en: The glowing adverts tantalized the children walking past the toy shop.
examples.cn: 闪烁的广告撩拨着路过玩具店的孩子们。

examples.en: She tantalized the audience with one chapter and published no more.
examples.cn: 她只给读者看了一章便吊足了胃口，之后不再发表。

examples.en: A tantalizing smell of garlic drifted from the kitchen.
examples.cn: 厨房里飘来一阵令人垂涎的蒜香。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摊塔了」——摊开塔里的宝物给你看，却锁着门不让进；这只是谐音联想，真正的来源是希腊神话中的国王名。

root: 由希腊神话国王坦塔洛斯（希腊语 Tantalos，拉丁语 Tantalus）之名加英语动词后缀 -ize 构成，核心义「把想要的东西摆在眼前却让够不着」；该神话人物名的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: From the myth of a fruit that withdraws come the senses of teasing, arousing appetite, promising and then denying, flirting, promising without fulfilment, and deliberate luring.
sensesIntro.cn: 由「果子会退开」这一神话场景，长出逗引、撩动食欲、许诺又反悔、调情、令人神往而不兑现以及刻意引诱等义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fruit hanging just above a hand that keeps missing it.
core.cn: 核心意象：果子悬在伸手总差一点的地方。

branches.en: The tease and the bait both move what is wanted out of reach.
branches.cn: 逗引与设饵都把想要之物挪出触及范围。

branches.en: A partial sample turns frustration into appetite.
branches.cn: 只给出一点样品，就把挫败转成了食欲。

branches.en: Hope raised and then dashed is the darker reading.
branches.cn: 希望被提起又被掐灭，是更阴暗的一面。

branches.en: The approach-and-retreat pattern becomes flirtation.
branches.cn: 「靠近又退开」的模式变成了调情。

branches.en: Smell and preview both promise more than they give.
branches.cn: 气味与预告都许诺了比它们实际给出的更多。

intro.en: Tantalize is a name plus a suffix, and the family it builds includes tantalizing, tantalizingly, tantalization, and tantalizer.
intro.cn: tantalize 是「专名加后缀」的构词，派生出一族词：tantalizing、tantalizingly、tantalization 与 tantalizer。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is the god name Tantalus, carried through myth and classical reference rather than through a root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层就是神名 Tantalus，这个词是通过神话与古典典故传入的，而不是通过某个词根。

items.meaning: to make or treat in the stated way
items.example: The suffix -ize turns the name into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 把这个专名变成了动词。

items.meaningCN: 用可望而不可即的东西逗引
items.example: Tantalize is the base verb.
items.exampleCN: tantalize 是基础动词。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms tantalizing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 tantalizing。

items.example: Tantalizing describes an attractive smell.
items.exampleCN: tantalizing 可以形容诱人的气味。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms tantalizingly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 tantalizingly。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或过程的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ation forms tantalization.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 tantalization。

items.example: Tantalization names the teasing act.
items.exampleCN: tantalization 指逗引的行为。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: The suffix -er forms tantalizer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 tantalizer。

items.meaning: one who or that which tantalizes
items.meaningCN: 撩拨者；吊人胃口的事物
items.example: Tantalizer can name a teasing person.
items.exampleCN: tantalizer 可指爱逗人的那种人。

latinEntries.meaning: the king punished with unattainable fruit and water
latinEntries.meaningCN: 因永远够不到果实与清水而受罚的国王

latinEntries.meaning: the earlier Greek form of the same name
latinEntries.meaningCN: 同一名字更早的希腊语形式
